The Railway Recruitment Cell (RRC), Kharagpur has published the Physical Efficiency Test (PET) result for CEN No. RRC-08/2024. The PET was conducted on 30 September 2026 at SERSA Stadium (Beighton Ground), Kharagpur. Two lists are available: a Qualified list and a Not Qualified list. Across both lists, 243 candidate numbers are listed as qualified and 115 as not qualified.

Organisation Railway Recruitment Cell, Kharagpur 
CEN No. RRC-08/2024
Stage Physical Efficiency Test (PET)
PET Date 30 September 2026
Venue SERSA Stadium (Beighton Ground), Kharagpur, West Bengal - 721301
Result Lists List of Qualified Candidates (3 pages) and List of Not Qualified Candidates (2 pages)

RRC Kharagpur PET Result 2026 - Direct Link

RRC Kharagpur PET result 2026 for CEN No. RRC-08/2024. This page gives the full qualified and not qualified candidate number lists, PET date and venue, a step-by-step way to check your result.

  • Direct Link to Check RRC Kharagpur PET Qualified Candidates List.
  • Direct Link to Check RRC Kharagpur PET Not Qualified Candidates List 

How to Check RRC Kharagpur PET Result 2026

  1. Keep your 16-digit candidate number ready. The lists do not say which of your documents carries this number, so match it with the number on your PET call letter or application record.
  2. Open the List of Qualified Candidates and search for your number. On a computer, press Ctrl+F and type the number. On a phone, use "Find in page".
  3. If your number is not in the qualified list, check the List of Not Qualified Candidates.
  4. If your number appears in neither list, contact the Railway Recruitment Cell, Kharagpur and ask about your status. Do not assume the result either way.

Important Instructions

  • The lists show candidate numbers only. Match all 16 digits carefully, because many numbers start with the same digits.
  • The file names of the two lists include the word "Male", but the list text itself does not mention gender. Check the official notice if you are unsure which list applies to you.
  • Qualifying in the PET does not by itself confirm final selection. The lists do not describe later stages.
  • Use the official PDFs as the final source. Counts and numbers on this page are a reproduction of the lists.
  • If your number is missing from both lists, contact the Railway Recruitment Cell, Kharagpur.

The Rajasthan Public Service Commission (RPSC), Ajmer, has released the result of the Veterinary Officer (Animal Husbandry Department) Competitive Exam-2025. The notice is dated 30 September 2026. It declares candidates successful in a Main List and a Reserve List, along with category-wise cut off marks.

RPSC Veterinary Officer Result 2026 - Quick Overview

Particular Details
Conducting Body Rajasthan Public Service Commission (RPSC), Ajmer
Post Name Veterinary Officer (Animal Husbandry Department)

Candidates in Reserve List 455

Official Website rpsc.rajasthan.gov.in

What Does the RPSC Veterinary Officer Notice Say?

Eligibility checking and document verification were done by the concerned department. The candidates were included provisionally in the scrutiny list issued on 16 June 2026.

  • Main List: After eligibility and document verification, the listed roll numbers are declared successful against the advertised posts. The merit rank is printed in brackets next to each roll number, for example, M-14.
  • Reserve List: Candidates in this list may be recommended for appointment if the department sends a demand within its prescribed time. Merit ranks here are printed as R-numbers.
  • (P) mark: A (P) next to a roll number means the result is provisional.

What Is the UPSSSC Havildar Instructor Eligibility Result?

The eligibility result is the first shortlisting stage of this recruitment. UPSSSC has not yet conducted a main exam for this post. Instead, the Commission has used the normalized scores of the UPSSSC PET 2025 to decide which candidates move on to the Main Examination.

Being on this list means you are eligible to appear in the next stage. It does not mean you are finally selected for the post.

JHTET Online Form 2026 : Educational Qualification 

Class  Eligibility 
Primary Level Teachers (Class 1 to 5)
  • Candidates must have passed 10+2 (Intermediate) with at least 50% marks (or 45% as per NCTE rules) along with or appearing in a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (BTC/D.El.Ed), or a 4-year B.El.Ed, or a 2-year Diploma in Special Education. Alternatively, candidates with a Bachelor’s degree and pursuing or completed a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education are also eligible.
Upper Primary Teacher (Class 6 to 8)
  • Candidates must meet any one of the following qualifications: a Bachelor’s degree along with or appearing in a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (BTC/D.El.Ed); or a Bachelor’s degree with at least 50% (or 45% as per NCTE rules) and B.Ed/L.T./Shiksha Shastri; or 10+2 with at least 50% and a 4-year B.El.Ed or B.A/B.Sc.Ed; or a Bachelor’s degree with at least 50% and B.Ed in Special Education; or a Master’s degree with 55% marks and a 3-year integrated B.Ed-M.Ed course.

ITBP Constable (GD) Sports Quota Recruitment 2026 Overview

Organisation Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force (ITBPF), Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India

Candidates must check the exact event/category vacancy relevant to them in the source PDF. Vacancies are tentative and may increase/decrease; unfilled vacancies in one discipline/category may be transferred to another at ITBPF's discretion. These vacancies are not open to physically handicapped persons or ex-servicemen.

ITBP Constable (GD) Sports Quota Eligibility

  • Educational Qualification: Matriculation or its equivalent from a recognized board
  • Nationality: Indian citizen, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan
  • Sports Qualification: Must have participated or won medal(s) in one of the recognized levels of competition (International, National, Inter-University, Khelo India Games, etc. – see marking scheme below) between 01.01.2024 and 01.11.2026
  • Candidates must possess all required educational and sports certificates on the date of recruitment; those without them are not eligible
  • Educational certificates from boards other than Central/State Boards must be accompanied by a Government notification declaring equivalence for Central Government service

OBC (NCL) certificate must be obtained within 3 years before the closing date (01.11.2026). Date of Birth is finalized based on the Matriculation/Higher Secondary certificate submitted; no subsequent change request is considered.

Weight: Proportionate to height and age as per the medical standards chart (Annexure-I).

Medical Standards

  • Minimum distance vision 6/6 and 6/9 in both eyes without correction (glasses/lenses not permitted); binocular vision required; colour vision tested by CP III (Ishihara)
  • Colour-blind candidates are not eligible
  • No knock-knees, flat foot, varicose veins, or squint; must be in good mental and bodily health
  • Tattoos: only religious symbols/figures/names permitted, on the left forearm (inner aspect) or dorsum of hands only, sized under ¼ of that body part

Also includes Dearness Allowance, Ration Money, Washing Allowance, Special Compensatory Allowance (border postings), free uniform, free accommodation/HRA, Transport Allowance, free Leave Pass, free medical facilities, and other admissible allowances. Pension under the New Restructured Defined Contributory Pension Scheme (w.e.f. 01.01.2004).

ITBP Constable (GD) Sports Quota Selection Process & Marking Scheme

Selection follows: Documentation → Physical Standard Test (PST) → Sports Trial Test (qualifying) → Merit List (based on sports achievement marks) → Detailed Medical Examination (DME) → Review Medical Examination (RME), if required. There is no written examination.

Sports Achievement Marking Scheme (Selected Rows)

Competition Gold Silver Bronze Participation
Olympic Games (Summer & Winter) 100 92 84 75
Asian Games 85 77 69 60
Commonwealth Games 80 72 64 55
World Championship/World Cup (Annual) 70 62 54 45
National Games / Senior National Championship 30 22 17 Not eligible
Junior National Championship 25 18 15 Not eligible
Inter-University / Khelo India University Games 20 13 11 Not eligible
Khelo India Youth/Winter Games 15 12 10 Not eligible
The official notification lists 18 competition tiers in total (including Youth Olympics, World Championship Quadrennial/Biennial, Junior World Championship, Asian Championship Quadrennial/Biennial/Annual, Junior Asian Championship, World University Games, and other MYA&S-cleared international events). Candidates get marks for only the single highest medal/participation secured in the 01.01.2024–01.11.2026 window.

Documentation, PST & Sports Trial Test

  • Documentation: Verification of original certificates (age, education, caste, sports achievement); identity/biometric verification is mandatory
  • Physical Standard Test (PST): Height, chest (male only) and weight checked against the standards above; over/underweight candidates are not debarred at this stage – final fitness decision rests with the Medical Officer at DME
  • Sports Trial Test: 40 marks, qualifying in nature, minimum cut-off 20 marks (does not count toward final merit); exempted for candidates who represented India in an International Sports Event with Department of Sports clearance
  • No appeal is entertained for re-conduct of the Sports Trial Test

Merit List & Tie-Breaking

  • Final merit is based purely on the sports achievement marking scheme (Documentation + PST + Sports Trial marks are not added to merit, only used for shortlisting/qualifying)
  • Tie-break order: (1) higher marks, (2) higher National-competition achievement if International achievements are equal, (3) younger candidate, (4) alphabetical order of name in English

Medical Examination

  • Detailed Medical Examination (DME) conducted per MHA's Uniform Guidelines for Recruitment Medical Examination (dated 20.05.2015, as amended)
  • Candidates declared unfit may opt for Review Medical Examination (RME) by giving written consent within 24 hours; the RME decision is final
  • Pregnant female candidates are declared temporarily unfit; their vacancy is held and they are re-examined 6 weeks after confinement, subject to a fitness certificate

How to Apply for ITBP Constable (GD) Sports Quota Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit recruitment.itbpolice.nic.in and create a candidate profile with a genuine, active e-mail ID and mobile number.
  2. Upload a copy of the certificate/document supporting your highest medal/position or highest level of sports participation in the advertised duration before applying – applications without this are rejected during scrutiny.
  3. Complete the online application form carefully.
  4. Pay the application fee online, if applicable to your category.
  5. Submit before the closing date: 01 November 2026, 11:59 PM. Offline applications are summarily rejected.

Application Fee

Category Fee
Male UR/OBC/EWS ₹100
Female (any category) / SC / ST Exempted (Nil)
Important: Fee once paid is non-refundable, and payment via any mode other than the ITBPF website leads to summary rejection.

Documents Required

  • Matriculation/10th class certificate (proof of date of birth)
  • Sports achievement certificate(s), signed by the competent awarding authority (National Federation Secretary, IOA, University Dean of Sports, or SAI, depending on the competition level)
  • OBC certificate (Annexure-III) with Non-Creamy-Layer declaration (Annexure-III(A)), SC/ST certificate (Annexure-IV), or EWS certificate valid for 2025-26 (Annexure-V), as applicable
  • No Objection Certificate (Annexure-II), for candidates in Government service
  • Certificate for height/chest relaxation (Annexure-VI), if claiming this relaxation
  • Domicile certificate issued by local revenue authorities (special format, Annexure-VI(A), for West Pakistani Refugees in J&K/Ladakh)
  • Four latest passport-size photographs (same as used in the online application)

Important Conditions

  • These vacancies are not open to physically challenged persons or ex-servicemen
  • Selected candidates must serve a minimum of 10 years in the Force; resigning earlier requires refunding 3 months' pay/allowances or training cost, whichever is higher
  • No TA/DA is admissible for travel to/from the recruitment venue; candidates should be prepared for a multi-day stay at their own arrangement and cost

The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) has released the notice for the Combined Higher Secondary Level (CHSL) Examination 2026, inviting online applications for Lower Division Clerk (LDC)/Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA) and Data Entry Operator (DEO)/DEO Grade 'A' posts. SSC CHSL Recruitment 2026 offers approximately 2,536 tentative vacancies across various Ministries, Departments, and Offices of the Government of India. Applications open on 07 September 2026 and close on 07 October 2026.

In short: SSC is recruiting for LDC/JSA and DEO posts under CHSL 2026, with about 2,536 tentative vacancies. Candidates who have passed Class 12 (or an equivalent exam) from a recognised board can apply. Online applications open on 07 September 2026 and close on 07 October 2026, with fee payment allowed until 08 October 2026. The application mode is online only, via the SSC website or the SSC mobile app, and the posts are located across various Central Government offices in India.

SSC CHSL Eligibility Criteria and Qualification

Eligibility for SSC CHSL Recruitment 2026 is assessed as on the cut-off date of 07 October 2026, and covers nationality, educational qualification, and age.

Nationality

A candidate must be a citizen of India, a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated from certain specified countries with the intention of settling permanently in India (candidates in the latter categories require an eligibility certificate from the Government of India).

SSC CHSL Qualification

Post Qualification Required
DEO/DEO Grade 'A' in Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, SSC, and Ministry of Culture 12th Standard pass in Science stream with Mathematics as a subject, from a recognised Board
LDC/JSA and DEO/DEO Grade 'A' (all other Departments/Ministries) 12th Standard pass or equivalent examination from a recognised Board or University

Candidates who have appeared for their Class 12 exam can also apply, but they must have the qualifying result declared on or before 07 October 2026. Only a declared result counts - a result "under process" does not meet the requirement.

SSC CHSL Age Limit

The age limit for SSC CHSL Recruitment 2026 is 18 to 27 years, reckoned as on 01 August 2026. This means candidates born not before 02 August 1999 and not later than 01 August 2008 are eligible to apply. Age relaxation is available as per government norms.

The application fee for SSC CHSL Recruitment 2026 is Rs. 100. Women candidates and candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwBD, and Ex-Servicemen (ESM) categories eligible for reservation are exempted from the fee.

SSC CHSL Selection Process

Selection for SSC CHSL Recruitment 2026 is through a Computer Based Examination conducted in two tiers.

Tier-I

Part Subject Questions/Marks
I English Language (Basic Knowledge) 25/50
II General Intelligence 25/50
III Quantitative Aptitude (Basic Arithmetic Skill) 25/50
IV General Awareness 25/50

Tier-I consists of objective type, multiple-choice questions only, with a total duration of 60 minutes and negative marking of 0.50 marks per wrong answer.

Tier-II

Tier-II is conducted in two sessions on the same day, comprising four sections: Section-I (Mathematical Abilities and Reasoning & General Intelligence), Section-II (English Language & Comprehension and General Awareness), Section-III (Computer Knowledge Test, qualifying in nature), and Section-IV (Skill Test/Typing Test for DEO and LDC/JSA posts respectively). It is mandatory to qualify all sections of Tier-II. There is negative marking of 1 mark per wrong answer in Sections I and II.

How to Apply for SSC CHSL Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official SSC website at ssc.gov.in or the "my SSC" mobile application.

  4. Opt for Aadhaar-based authentication during OTR, if desired, to simplify photo/ID requirements at the exam venue.
  5. Upload the required details and capture your photograph as per the instructions in the application module.
  6. Pay the application fee online (if applicable) before 08 October 2026.
  7. Submit the form and keep a printout for your records.

  • The correction window (14–16 October 2026) allows a maximum of two modifications/re-submissions to the application; only applications with fee received (or fee-exempted) are eligible for correction.
  • Applications remaining "Incomplete" due to non-receipt of fee will be summarily rejected.
  • The Tier-I and Tier-II exam schedule will be announced separately.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates applying for IFFCO Agriculture Graduate Trainee Recruitment 2026 should meet the following educational and language requirements.

  • Educational Qualification: Four-year B.Sc. (Agriculture) full-time regular degree from a University/Institute recognized by the UGC/AICTE.

  • Language: Candidates must be well versed in reading, writing and speaking the regional language of the State for which the application is made. Knowing one or more languages will be an added advantage, and knowledge of Hindi is desirable.
  • Training Period: Selected candidates will undergo a training period of one year.

  • Stipend during Training: Rs. 33,300/- per month (as per the rules of the organisation, at present).

When the prescribed number of SC or ST candidates are not available, those reserved training places may be filled by the other of the two (SC by ST, or vice versa); if still unfilled, they may be filled by candidates not belonging to SC/ST. Similarly, seats remaining unfilled by OBC/EWS candidates will be filled by unreserved category candidates. Reserved PwBD and Ex-servicemen seats are not separate or additional - they are already included within the total slots shown for each trade.

NWR Act Apprentice Eligibility Criteria

NWR Act Apprentice Qualification

Candidates must have passed the Class 10 examination or its equivalent (under the 10+2 examination system) with a minimum of 50% marks in aggregate (no rounding off) from a recognised Board, and must also possess a National Trade Certificate (NTC) in the notified trade, issued by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT) or State Council for Vocational Training (SCVT). Candidates should have the requisite educational/technical qualification from a recognised Board/Government University/Institute as on the date of submission of the application; those awaiting results of their final exams should not apply.

NWR Act Apprentice Reservation Details

Candidates claiming SC/ST reservation must produce a caste certificate in the Central Government format at the time of Document Verification. OBC candidates must produce a caste certificate and a Non-Creamy Layer Certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026, in the Central Government format, along with an OBC declaration. EWS candidates must produce an EWS certificate in the prescribed format. Ex-servicemen and Armed Forces Personnel (or their children) must produce a discharge certificate, or an Armed Forces serving certificate in the case of children of serving personnel, at the time of Document Verification. Ex-servicemen candidates are placed in their appropriate category (UR/SC/ST/OBC); if UR vacancies under the Ex-servicemen quota are unavailable, Ex-servicemen belonging to communities where vacancies are available will be considered.

NWR Act Apprentice Age Limit

Particulars Age
Minimum Age 15 years (completed)
Maximum Age 24 years (not completed)

NWR Act Apprentice Age Relaxation

  • SC/ST candidates: 5 years' relaxation in upper age limit.
  • OBC candidates: 3 years' relaxation in upper age limit.
  • Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD): 10 years' relaxation in upper age limit.
  • Ex-servicemen: relaxable by up to an additional 10 years, to the extent of service rendered in the Defence Forces plus 3 years, provided a minimum of 6 months' continuous service was completed (this does not apply to ex-servicemen who have already joined government service on the civil side after availing ex-servicemen status for that engagement).

NWR Act Apprentice Stipend & Training

Training period and stipend will be as per the extant rules and directives issued by the Railway Board from time to time; a specific stipend amount is not stated in this notification. No hostel accommodation will be provided - selected candidates must make their own arrangements during training, as per the Apprentices Act, 1961, and will be released upon completion of training. Before commencing training, the selected candidate (or their guardian, if a minor) must enter into a Contract of Apprenticeship with the employer.

NWR Act Apprentice Application Fee

Category Application Fee (Non-refundable)
All candidates except those listed below ₹100
SC/ST, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), Women Nil

Fee payment is made online through the payment gateway integrated with the online application, using debit card, credit card, Internet Banking, or similar modes, after the application form is completed and verified for correctness; no change/edit is allowed after fee payment. Any transaction charges for online payment are borne by the candidate. On successful payment, an e-receipt is generated, which should be printed and retained.

NWR Act Apprentice Selection Process

Selection is based on a merit list prepared for all candidates who apply against the notification, calculated as the simple average of the percentage of marks in Matriculation (minimum 50% aggregate) and the percentage of marks in ITI, in the trade in which apprenticeship is sought.

  • For Matriculation percentage, marks obtained by the candidate in all subjects are considered - not the marks of any single subject or group of subjects.
  • For ITI percentage, marks mentioned in the provisional/final certificate are considered.
  • In case two candidates have the same marks, the older candidate is preferred; if the date of birth is also the same, the candidate who passed the Matriculation exam earlier is considered first.
  • The final merit list is prepared division/unit-wise, trade-wise, and community-wise, equal to the number of slots, in descending order of the percentage of marks obtained.
  • Candidates finally enlisted are subject to verification of original testimonials and production of a medical certificate (as per the notification's Annexure-IV).

Candidates should note that no centralised merit list is formed - each unit's merit list is prepared separately based on candidates who applied for that specific unit.

Medical Fitness

Selected candidates must produce a medical certificate in the prescribed format at the time of Document Verification, signed by a Government-authorised Gazetted Doctor not below the rank of Assistant Surgeon of a Central/State Hospital. Standards of fitness for Persons with Disability are also specified in the notification, covering Locomotor Disability/Cerebral Palsy (not less than 40% relevant disability), Hearing Impairment (loss of 60 decibels or more in the better ear, including Deaf, Dumb, or Deaf & Dumb candidates), and other benchmark disability categories as defined in the notification.

How to Apply for NWR Act Apprentice Recruitment 2026

NWR Act Apprentice Apply Online

Candidates must apply online only, by visiting www.rrcjaipur.in, between 7 October 2026 and 6 November 2026 (23:59 hrs). No physical copy of the application needs to be sent to RRC, and any physical copy received will not be given cognisance. The broad process is:

  1. Log in and fill personal details: Log on to the RRC/Jaipur website and carefully fill in personal details/bio-data, including a valid 12-digit Aadhaar Card number (the original Aadhaar card must be produced at Document Verification).
  2. Select one unit only: Candidates must choose only one Division/Unit from the 8 listed, and should carefully check that a training slot exists for their specific ITI trade in that unit before selecting it, since changes are not allowed after final submission.
  3. Upload photograph: A recent colour photograph (3.5 cm × 3.5 cm, not older than 3 months, JPG/JPEG format, 100 DPI, file size 20 KB–70 KB) with a clear front view, without cap or sunglasses.
  4. Upload signature: A scanned signature (3.5 cm × 2.5 cm, JPG/JPEG format, 100 DPI, file size 20 KB–30 KB).
  5. Pay the application fee: Pay the applicable fee (see Fee section above) through the integrated payment gateway, after verifying that all application details are correct, since no changes are allowed after payment.
  6. Download and retain printout: After successful submission, download and keep a printout of the application; this will be required at the time of Document Verification, if shortlisted.

Candidates must ensure their name, father's name, and date of birth exactly match their Matriculation (or equivalent) certificate - any deviation found during Document Verification will lead to cancellation of candidature and debarment. Candidates should also provide an active mobile number and valid email ID, since all important communication will be sent via SMS/email.

NWR Act Apprentice Important Instructions

  • Candidates may apply for only one unit; submitting more than one application with different particulars (name, father's name, community, photo, qualification, email, or mobile number) will result in summary rejection of all such applications.
  • The decision of the Railway administration on all matters relating to eligibility, acceptance or rejection of applications, and mode of selection is final.
  • Imparting training on the Railway does not confer any right to absorption/employment on the Railway after successful completion of training; per the Apprenticeship Rules, 1992, it is not obligatory for the employer to offer employment, nor for the apprentice to accept it, upon completion of training.
  • No correspondence regarding engagement will be entertained.
  • Canvassing in any form will disqualify the candidature, and no correspondence will be entertained in this regard.
  • Candidates should ensure they fulfil all eligibility criteria before applying; if erroneously engaged, such candidates will be summarily dismissed without notice at any stage.
  • For help with online submission or printing of the application, candidates can call the helpline number published on the website from 7 October 2026, available 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM (except Sundays and holidays) until the last date of application.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The CSIR-Traditional Knowledge Digital Library Unit (CSIR-TKDL Unit), New Delhi, has released Advertisement No. TKDL/08/2026 inviting applications for Senior Project Associate and Project Associate-I positions. A total of 50 positions have been notified across Delhi, Jammu, Srinagar, Leh, Palampur, Chennai and Hyderabad, in disciplines such as Information Technology, Data Science, Ayurveda, Unani, Sowa Rigpa, Siddha, Patent, Sanskrit and Yoga.

The positions are for the project titled "Information systems of traditional knowledge for protection and promotion" (TKDL-TK, MLP002639). The engagement is purely temporary and on contract basis, initially up to 31 March 2027 and extendable up to a maximum of 31 March 2031, co-terminus with the project. Extension beyond 31 March 2027 is subject to review by a Review Committee.

Eligible candidates must apply online through www.csir.res.in on or before 12 October 2026, 5:00 PM. Selection is through a written test held at the respective posting location between 14 October 2026 and 30 October 2026, followed by an interview of shortlisted candidates. Read this article for the complete details on post-wise vacancies, eligibility, salary, age limit, important dates, selection process and how to apply for CSIR TKDL Project Associate Recruitment 2026.

CSIR TKDL Project Associate Recruitment 2026 Overview

Company Name Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - Traditional Knowledge Digital Library Unit (CSIR-TKDL)
Post Name Senior Project Associate, Project Associate-I
No of Posts 50
Salary Senior Project Associate: Rs. 42,000/- + HRA; Project Associate-I: Rs. 31,000/- + HRA or Rs. 25,000/- + HRA
Qualification Varies by post: B.E./B.Tech/MCA (IT/Data Science), BAMS, BUMS, BSMS, Sowa Rigpa degree, Master's in Chemical/Biological Sciences/Bioinformatics/Cheminformatics, Sanskrit or Yoga. See Eligibility Criteria for details.
Age Limit Up to 40 years (Senior Project Associate) and up to 35 years (Project Associate-I)
Start Date for Apply  Not specified in the notification
Last Date for Apply  12-10-2026 (up to 5:00 PM)
Official Website www.csir.res.in

CSIR-TKDL Unit is engaged in the protection and preservation of India's traditional knowledge present in ancient texts, including the Indian Systems of Medicine, by converting the information into structured format and modern languages. It aims to prevent misappropriation of traditional knowledge through the grant of intellectual property rights. The Unit functions under the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), an autonomous body under the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, Ministry of Science and Technology.

CSIR TKDL Vacancy 2026 Notification PDF

Candidates should download and read the CSIR TKDL Jobs 2026 notification PDF carefully to check vacancy details, eligibility, age limit, and application instructions. The notification also includes important dates and selection process details. The direct download link is available in the Important Links section below.

Download CSIR TKDL Job 2026 Notification PDF

CSIR TKDL Project Associate Recruitment 2026 Vacancy Details 

A total of 50 positions are notified. The posting location may change as per project requirements and availability of candidates. A panel of waitlisted candidates will also be constituted to fill vacancies in the near future, and this panel will be valid for one year.

Posting Locations

  • Delhi: CSIR-TKDL Unit, 14, Satsang Vihar Marg, Spl. Institutional Area, New Delhi - 110067

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfil the essential and other stipulated criteria as on 12-10-2026. Candidates who are in the final semester or whose results are awaited are not eligible. Mere fulfilment of the minimum qualification does not confer any right to be called for interview, and candidature is purely provisional. Post-wise qualifications are given below.

Information Technology (TKD3901, TKJ3901, TKC3901, TKH3901, TKL3901, TKS3901, TKP3901)

  • TKD3901 (Senior Project Associate, IT): Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Technology in Computer Science/Information Technology or equivalent, or MCA, with three years' experience in R&D in Industrial and Academic Institutions or S&T Organisations and scientific activities and services; OR ME/M.Tech in Engineering or Technology in Computer Science/Information Technology or equivalent with two years' experience in R&D in the same settings.
  • TKD3901 Experience: Core Java and above, advanced Java, J2EE, SQL queries, implementing MVC architecture using Spring and Hibernate frameworks, Postgres database, JavaScript, AJAX, JSON, AngularJS, Bootstrap, jQuery, JDBC and RESTful; exposure to JBoss and Tomcat servers; familiarity with IDEs such as NetBeans/Eclipse; proficiency in SQL coding using procedures/functions, cursors, triggers and packages; understanding of code versioning tools such as Git. Knowledge of data science applications is an added advantage. OR proficiency in engineering, administering and managing multiple relational database flavours (e.g. Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL) including database migration.
  • TKC3901 and TKH3901 (Project Associate-I, IT-Data Science): Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Technology in Computer Science/Information Technology/Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning/Data Science/Electronics or equivalent, or MCA.
  • TKC3901 and TKH3901 Desirable skills: Proficiency in one or more of Core Java, J2EE, EJB; strong knowledge of Python, SQL, machine learning, and data analysis and visualization tools; understanding of statistical modelling and predictive analytics; familiarity with cloud platforms and big data technologies; good communication and problem-solving skills.
  • TKJ3901, TKL3901, TKS3901 and TKP3901 (Project Associate-I, IT): Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Technology in Computer Science/Information Technology or equivalent, or MCA.
  • TKJ3901, TKL3901, TKS3901 and TKP3901 Desirable skills: Proficiency in one or more of Core Java, J2EE, EJB, Enterprise Java, Spring, Jasper Reports, Struts, Hibernate, Maven, REST, SOAP and an IDE such as Eclipse/NetBeans/IntelliJ IDEA, with working knowledge of relational databases (e.g. SQL Server, PostgreSQL); OR proficiency in installation, configuration, administration and troubleshooting of RHEL7 or above, nginx and Apache Tomcat, with knowledge of RHEL OS upgradation, performance tuning, licensing, patching, vulnerability remediation, Java-based web servers, server hardening and server backups.

Ayurveda, Unani, Sowa Rigpa and Siddha

  • TKD3902 (Senior Project Associate, Ayurveda): BAMS (Ayurveda) or equivalent with three years' experience in R&D in Industrial and Academic Institutions or S&T Organisations and scientific activities and services; OR MD (Ayurveda) or equivalent with two years' experience in the same. Candidates with proficiency in Sanskrit or Malayalam will be preferred.
  • TKD3903 and TKJ3902 (Project Associate-I, Ayurveda): BAMS (Ayurveda) from a recognized University or equivalent.
  • TKH3902 and TKS3902 (Project Associate-I, Unani): BUMS (Unani) from a recognized University or equivalent. Candidates with proficiency in Arabic and/or Persian will be preferred.
  • TKL3902 (Senior Project Associate, Sowa Rigpa): Bachelor's degree in Sowa Rigpa medicine or equivalent with three years' experience in R&D in Industrial and Academic Institutions or S&T Organisations and scientific activities and services; OR MD (Sowa Rigpa) or equivalent with two years' experience in the same.
  • TKL3903 and TKP3902 (Project Associate-I, Sowa Rigpa): Bachelor's degree in Sowa Rigpa medicine from a recognized University or equivalent.
  • TKC3902 (Senior Project Associate, Siddha): BSMS (Siddha) or equivalent with three years' experience in R&D in Industrial and Academic Institutions or S&T Organisations and scientific activities and services; OR MD (Siddha) or equivalent with two years' experience in the same.
  • TKC3903 (Project Associate-I, Siddha): BSMS (Siddha) from a recognized University or equivalent.

Patent, Sanskrit and Yoga

  • TKD3904 and TKH3903 (Senior Project Associate, Patent): Master's degree in Chemical or Biological Sciences/Bioinformatics/Cheminformatics or equivalent with three years' experience in R&D in Industrial and Academic Institutions or S&T Organisations and scientific activities and services; OR Doctoral degree in Chemical or Biological Science or equivalent with two years' experience in the same. Desirable: experience in patent analytics/informatics or PG Diploma in IPR, and good written and oral skills in English.
  • TKD3905 and TKH3904 (Project Associate-I, Patent): Master's degree in Chemical or Biological Sciences/Bioinformatics/Cheminformatics or equivalent. Desirable: proficiency in patent analytics/informatics or PG Diploma in IPR, and good written and oral skills in English.
  • TKD3906 (Senior Project Associate, Sanskrit): Master's degree in Sanskrit or equivalent with three years' experience in R&D in Industrial and Academic Institutions or S&T Organisations and scientific activities and services; OR Doctoral degree in Sanskrit or equivalent with two years' experience in the same. Desirable: knowledge of traditional medical texts and familiarity with medical terms including diseases, plant names, etc.
  • TKD3907 (Project Associate-I, Yoga): Master's degree in Yoga from a recognized University or equivalent.

Other Requirements

  • Preference will be given to candidates with proficiency in applicable languages, and working knowledge of computers and commonly used software.
  • Candidates who are currently employed must furnish a no-objection certificate from the current employer at the time of joining.

Salary/Stipend

The monthly emoluments for CSIR TKDL Project Associate Recruitment 2026 depend on the post and the qualifying exams cleared by the candidate:

  • Senior Project Associate: Rs. 42,000/- per month + HRA
  • Project Associate-I: Rs. 31,000/- per month + HRA for candidates who have qualified (a) a National Eligibility Test - CSIR-UGC NET including lectureship (Assistant Professorship) or GATE, or (b) a selection process through national level examinations conducted by Central Government Departments and their Agencies and Institutions
  • Project Associate-I (others): Rs. 25,000/- per month + HRA for candidates who do not fall under the above category
  • The engagement is purely temporary and on contract basis, initially up to 31 March 2027 and up to a maximum of 31 March 2031, co-terminus with the project.

Age Limit (as on 12-10-2026)

The age limits are as follows. These limits are relaxable for candidates of statutory groups as per CSIR/Government of India rules (SC/ST/OBC/PwD/woman, as per the notification).

  • Senior Project Associate: Maximum 40 years
  • Project Associate-I: Maximum 35 years
  • Minimum Age: Not specified in the notification

Application Fee

  • The notification does not mention any application fee for CSIR TKDL Project Associate Recruitment 2026.
  • No TA/DA will be paid for attending the test/interview.

Important Dates

Candidates should note the following dates. The written test will be held at the posting location of the post applied for, on the date and time mentioned against the post code.

  • Last Date for Online Application: 12-10-2026 (up to 5:00 PM)
  • Written Test - Information Technology posts (TKD3901, TKJ3901, TKC3901, TKH3901, TKL3901, TKS3901, TKP3901): 14-10-2026
  • Written Test - Sowa Rigpa posts (TKL3902, TKL3903, TKP3902): 15-10-2026
  • Written Test - Unani posts (TKH3902, TKS3902): 16-10-2026
  • Written Test - Ayurveda posts (TKD3902, TKD3903, TKJ3902): 22-10-2026
  • Written Test - Patent posts (TKD3904, TKD3905, TKH3903, TKH3904): 23-10-2026
  • Written Test - Siddha posts (TKC3902, TKC3903): 26-10-2026
  • Written Test - Sanskrit and Yoga posts (TKD3906, TKD3907): 30-10-2026

Selection Process

Selection will be through a written test followed by an interview of shortlisted candidates.

  • Candidates must present themselves at the posting location mentioned against the post code for the written test on the stated date and time.
  • The results of the written test will be declared on the same day.
  • The interview of shortlisted candidates will take place in hybrid mode (offline and online), either on the day of the written test or on another day, as informed after the written test. If the Committee so desires, candidates will be asked to appear in person and will be informed accordingly.
  • Candidates are requested to wait after their written test for results/instructions unless informed otherwise.
  • Candidates must bring the following at the time of the written test: original certificates/testimonials, two copies of self-attested photographs, a set of self-attested copies of certificates/testimonials in support of age, qualification, marks obtained and experience (if any), and a neatly typed bio-data on A4 paper.
  • Candidates belonging to statutory categories must bring the original category certificate issued by the competent authority, along with self-attested copies.

Terms of Engagement

  • The tenure is co-terminus with the project and, under no circumstances, will exceed six years cumulatively, inclusive of all CSIR postings. Performance will be reviewed periodically, and staff not found up to the mark may be terminated without assigning any reason.
  • The contract confers no right to continuation beyond the tenure, absorption or regularization in CSIR. It may be terminated at any time with one month's notice from either side or one month's stipend in lieu thereof.
  • Project staff will be governed by the CSIR guidelines on engagement of project staff, as amended from time to time.
  • The posting location may change as per requirement, and project staff may be required to travel as per need.
  • The Head, CSIR-TKDL Unit may increase/decrease the number of positions or cancel the recruitment process at any stage, and his decision is final and binding. Canvassing in any form will render the candidate disqualified.

How to Apply

Eligible candidates can apply for CSIR TKDL Project Associate Recruitment 2026 through online mode only. Follow the steps below:

  1. Visit the official website, www.csir.res.in, and open the online application form for the advertisement TKDL/08/2026.
  2. Fill in all the details related to educational qualification, statutory category, experience, etc. Candidates who wish to apply for more than one post must apply separately for each position.
  3. Upload scanned copies of the original documents: certificates establishing educational qualifications (matriculation onwards), age, statutory category (for SC/ST/OBC/PwD/EWS candidates), experience certificate (if any), list of publications/patents (if any) and detailed bio-data. Candidature will be summarily rejected if these are not uploaded.
  4. Submit the application on or before 12-10-2026, 5:00 PM.
  5. Keep the generated application number for future correspondence.
  6. Report at the posting location on the test date and time with the original documents, self-attested copies, photographs and bio-data.

Incomplete applications or applications received through any other mode will not be accepted. For queries, contact 011-26851136 or [email protected]. For technical problems while submitting the online form, write to [email protected].

Last Date for Apply  28-10-2026 (up to 11:55 PM)
Official Website www.sci.gov.in

The advertisement states that the number of posts may change due to administrative exigencies and/or the requirement of the Registry, with the approval of the Competent Authority. The Registry also reserves the right to cancel, restrict, enlarge, modify or alter the selection process, if need arises, without issuing any notice.

Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026 Vacancy Details 

The Supreme Court of India has notified 250 tentative vacancies for the post of Junior Court Assistant. The post is a Group-B Non-Gazetted post placed in Level 6 of the Pay Matrix.

S. No. Post Name No. of Posts
1 Junior Court Assistant (Group-B Non-Gazetted, Level 6) 250 (tentative)

The category-wise (UR/SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD) breakup of the 250 vacancies is not specified in the advertisement. The benefit of reservation will be in accordance with Rule 4A of the Supreme Court Officers and Servants (Conditions of Service and Conduct) Rules, 1961.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates applying for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026 should ensure that they fulfil the prescribed qualification and eligibility conditions as on 01-09-2026. Admission at all stages of the examination is purely provisional, and eligibility documents will be verified at the time of document verification.

  • Nationality: Candidates must be Indian citizens.
  • Educational Qualification: Bachelor's degree of a recognized University in India.
  • Computer and Typing Skills: Knowledge of computer operation with a typing speed of 35 w.p.m. in computer.
  • Employed Candidates: Candidates working in Central/State Government Departments, Nationalized Banks or Public Sector Undertakings must submit a 'No Objection Certificate' from their employer at the time of document verification.
  • Candidates Getting Employment After Applying: A candidate who is not employed at the time of application but gets employment during or after the examination process must immediately inform the Branch Officer, Recruitment Cell, at [email protected], failing which an adverse inference will be drawn by the Registry.
  • If, at any time before or after the tests/interview, a candidate is found not to fulfil the prescribed qualification or any eligibility condition, the candidature will stand cancelled without notice.

Salary/Stipend

Selected Junior Court Assistants will be placed in Level 6 of the Pay Matrix. The salary details given in the notification are as follows:

  • Pay Level: Level 6 of the Pay Matrix (Group-B Non-Gazetted post)
  • Initial Basic Pay: Rs. 35,400/- per month
  • Allowances: Plus allowances (the specific allowances are not mentioned in the advertisement)

Age Limit (as on 01-09-2026)

The age of candidates will be counted as on 01-09-2026. Candidates must be at least 18 years old and not more than 30 years old, subject to the relaxations below.

  • Minimum Age: 18 years
  • Maximum Age: 30 years
  • Usual age relaxation is admissible to candidates belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes (Non-Creamy Layer), Physically Challenged and Ex-servicemen, as per the Government of India's rules.
  • Relaxation up to a maximum of five years, over and above the prescribed upper age limit of thirty years, is admissible to dependents of freedom fighters.
  • There is no upper age limit for Departmental candidates of the Registry of the Supreme Court of India.
  • No age relaxation will be allowed to candidates working in other Government Departments/Public Sector Undertakings/Nationalized Banks, etc.

To avoid any confusion regarding age eligibility, candidates can use our Age Calculator to calculate their exact age based on the prescribed cut-off date before applying.

Application Fee

Candidates have to pay the application fee online while applying. The fee is non-refundable under any circumstances, and no postal application form or fee in any other form will be accepted.

  • General/Unreserved Category: Rs. 1,500/- plus bank charges
  • SC/ST/OBC (Non-Creamy Layer)/Ex-Servicemen/Physically Challenged: Rs. 750/- plus bank charges
  • Payment Mode: Online only, through the payment gateway provided by UCO Bank.
  • Answer Key Objection Fee: Rs. 100/- per objection, refunded to the candidate if the objection is found to be valid.

Important Dates

Candidates should note the following dates for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026. The dates for the Typing Speed Test, Written Test and Interview will be notified on www.sci.gov.in and also sent by SMS and e-mail to the registered mobile number and e-mail ID.

  • Date of Advertisement: 30-09-2026
  • Start Date for Online Application: 07-10-2026
  • Last Date for Online Application: 28-10-2026 (up to 11:55 PM)
  • Objective Type Test: 20-11-2026 (tentative)
  • Answer Keys Upload: 22-11-2026
  • Objection Window for Answer Keys: 22-11-2026 to 23-11-2026, till 11:55 PM (tentative)
  • Typing Speed Test, Written Test (Descriptive) and Interview: To be notified

Selection Process

The selection of Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant will be made through the following four stages. Candidates have to appear in all the tests, and the minimum qualifying marks must be secured in each.

S. No. Details of Tests Duration Maximum Marks Minimum Qualifying Marks
1 Objective Type Test (Multiple Choice Questions), 100 questions 1½ hours 100 50
2 Typing Speed Test on Computer, in English Language (minimum speed 35 w.p.m.) 10 minutes 50 25
3 Written Test (Descriptive) in English Language 2 hours 100 50
4 Interview Not specified 25 13

Objective Type Test Pattern (100 Questions)

  • General English including comprehension section: 20 questions
  • General Aptitude: 15 questions
  • General Knowledge: 15 questions
  • Provisions relating to Judiciary in the Constitution of India: 15 questions
  • Supreme Court Rules, 2013: 10 questions
  • Supreme Court Officers and Servants (Conditions of Service and Conduct) Rules, 1961: 10 questions
  • Computer Knowledge: 15 questions
  • There is negative marking of 0.25 marks for each incorrect answer.
  • Answer keys will be uploaded on 22-11-2026. Objections may be sent through online mode only, and the decision of the competent Authority on objections will be final.

Typing Speed Test and Written Test

  • Typing Speed Test: mistakes allowed are 3% of the total words typed. An error in respect of a word/figure is treated as a full mistake. A wrong typing of a capital letter for a small letter or vice-versa, or an omitted, added or substituted punctuation mark, is treated as a half mistake.
  • Typing Speed Test on Computer is mandatory to qualify. Answer sheets of the Written Test (Descriptive) will be evaluated only for candidates who qualify the Typing Speed Test.
  • Written Test (Descriptive) in English consists of a Comprehension passage, Precis Writing and Essay Writing.

Shortlisting for Next Stages

  • If a large number of candidates qualify in the Objective Type Test by securing the minimum qualifying 50 marks or more, candidates will be shortlisted on the merit list in the ratio of 1:10 against the number of tentative vacancies for the Typing Speed Test and Written Test.
  • Candidates who qualify in all three tests (Objective Type Test, Typing Speed Test and Written Test) will be called for interview in the ratio of 1:3 against the number of tentative vacancies.

Test Centres

  • The Objective Type Test will be conducted in the cities listed in Annexure-A of the advertisement (131 test centres across states and union territories, including Delhi/NCR). Candidates have to select cities in the order of preference, and the Registry may shift candidates to other cities or increase/decrease test centres for administrative reasons.
  • The Typing Speed Test on Computer and the Written Test (Descriptive) will be conducted in Delhi/NCR.
  • The Interview will be conducted either online or in physical mode in Delhi, as directed by the competent Authority.
  • No request for change of city/test centre or date(s) of tests/interview will be entertained. No TA/DA is payable for appearing in the tests/interview.

How to Apply

Eligible candidates can apply for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026 through online mode only. Follow the steps below once the application link is activated on 07-10-2026:

  1. Visit the official website of the Supreme Court of India, www.sci.gov.in, and open the Recruitment link for Junior Court Assistant.
  2. Register and fill in the online Application Form. The Name, Father's name, Mother's name and Date of Birth must be entered exactly as in the High School Certificate/Xth Board Examination or equivalent certificate. Any change in name or surname must be supported by a Gazette Notification.
  3. Select the Objective Type Test cities in the order of preference.
  4. Upload the scanned copies of a recent photograph, signature and requisite documents: Class Xth, Class XIIth and Graduation Certificates, caste/community certificate (in case of reserved category candidates) and disability certificate (if applicable).
  5. Furnish the Undertaking that you have read and understood the terms and conditions of the advertisement and will abide by them.
  6. Pay the application fee online as per the instructions displayed on the payment link.
  7. Submit the Application Form on or before 28-10-2026 (11:55 PM), preview it and take a printout for your records. The printout need not be sent to the Registry.
  8. Retain the Application Number carefully, as it is required to generate the Admit Card and for any other information regarding the tests/interview.

Important Instructions

  • Application Forms that do not comply with the instructions will be summarily rejected. An application once submitted cannot be withdrawn or modified, and no request for change of category will be entertained.
  • If a candidate submits more than one Application Form, only the form with the latest Application Number will be considered.
  • If any information furnished is found incorrect/false, the candidature will be cancelled without notice. Candidates found guilty of impersonation or of submitting false or fabricated documents will be disqualified, prosecuted and debarred from future appointment in the Registry.
  • Candidates should keep a valid personal e-mail ID and mobile number active throughout the recruitment process. No Admit Cards will be sent by post; candidates must download them from the Supreme Court website.
  • Candidates should visit the Recruitment link on the Supreme Court website regularly for updates.
  • Persons with Disabilities will get concessions/facilities as per the Office Memorandum No. F.No.P-13013/75/2023-Policy-DD-III dated 01-08-2025 of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. The scribe facility can be availed by filling in the proforma Annexure-I or Annexure-IA with the relevant certificate(s). The scribe's qualification must be a minimum of two and a maximum of three academic years below the minimum qualification for the examination, and an 'own scribe' cannot be a candidate in the same examination or act as scribe for more than one candidate.
  • In case of any dispute, the jurisdiction will be Delhi.

DSSSB Combined Examination 2026 Overview

DSSSB Combined Exam 2026 Vacancy Details (Post-wise & Category-wise)

233 Senior PA + Personal Assistant
174 Jr. Judicial Assistant + Process Server
641 Total Posts
Post / Department Total PwBD ESM
Senior Personal Assistant – District & Sessions Courts 27 07 –

Note: Vacancies are tentative and based on inputs from the indenting departments, and may increase or decrease. PwBD suitability differs by post – e.g., Senior PA/PA is suitable only for Locomotor categories (OL, BL, LC, Dw, AAV, SD/SI without neurological dysfunction), while Junior Judicial Assistant, Process Server and Peon/Orderly/Dak Peon are suitable for a wider range including Blindness/Low Vision, Deaf/Hard of Hearing, and certain Autism/Intellectual/Learning Disability/Mental Illness categories, as specified for each post in the official notification.

DSSSB Combined Exam 2026 Eligibility (Post-wise)

Post Essential Qualification
Senior Personal Assistant Graduate with Shorthand speed of 110 wpm and Typing speed of 40 wpm
Personal Assistant (both Courts) Graduate with Shorthand speed of 100 wpm, Typing speed of 40 wpm, and knowledge of computers
Junior Judicial Assistant (both Courts) Graduate with typing speed of not less than 40 wpm on computer
Process Server (both Courts) Matriculation pass or equivalent from a recognized board/Higher Secondary, with a valid LMV driving licence and 2 years' unblemished driving experience
Peon/Orderly/Dak Peon (both Courts) Matriculation pass or equivalent from a recognized board
  • Citizenship: Candidate must be a citizen of India as defined in the Constitution of India or any law made by Parliament to regulate citizenship rights
  • Educational qualification/experience is determined as on the crucial/cut-off date: 04.11.2026

DSSSB Combined Exam 2026 Age Limit

All posts: Minimum 18 years, maximum 27 years, as on 01.06.2026 (born not earlier than 02.06.1999 and not later than 01.06.2008).

Age Relaxation (Group B & C Posts)

Category Relaxation
SC/ST 5 years
OBC 3 years
PwBD + UR/EWS 10 years
PwBD + SC/ST 15 years
PwBD + OBC 13 years
Government Employees (3+ years regular service) Not applicable – DDC Rules, 2012 (Rule 7) provide no age relaxation for this category
Ex-Servicemen Period of military service plus 3 years (maximum up to age 55)
Date of Birth as recorded in the Matriculation/Secondary School certificate (or equivalent) available at the time of application is final; no subsequent change request is entertained.

DSSSB Combined Exam 2026 Pay Scale

Post Pay Scale Group
Senior Personal Assistant ₹9,300–34,800 + Grade Pay ₹4,800 Group-B (Non-Gazetted)
Personal Assistant ₹9,300–34,800 + Grade Pay ₹4,600 Group-B (Non-Gazetted)

DSSSB Combined Exam 2026 Selection Process

Separate examinations are held for each post code. Minimum qualifying marks (MCQ/Descriptive stages): UR/EWS – 50%, OBC(Delhi)/SC/ST/PwBD/ESM – 45%. Each MCQ carries 1 mark, with negative marking of 0.25 for each wrong answer.

Senior Personal Assistant & Personal Assistant (Post Code 805/26)

Tier Format Marks / Detail
Tier-I MCQ (shortlisting) 90 marks, 90 min – English & Comprehension (50), GK (20), General Intelligence (20); up to 25× vacancies shortlisted
Tier-II Descriptive (English) 75 marks, 90 min – Essay 250 words (30), Grammar (25), Translation 20 words (20); up to 10× vacancies shortlisted for skill test
Tier-III Skill Test (qualifying) Senior PA: 550-word dictation (5 min) + 40-min transcription, max 22 errors (4%). PA: 500-word dictation + 40-min transcription, max 20 errors (4%). Typing @ 40 wpm for both.
Tier-IV Interview 10 marks, no minimum qualifying marks; conducted by Delhi District Courts; final merit on Tier-II + Tier-IV combined

Junior Judicial Assistant (Post Code 806/26)

Tier Format Marks / Detail
Tier-I MCQ (shortlisting) 120 marks, 120 min – English & Comprehension (60), GK (30), General Intelligence (30); up to 25× vacancies shortlisted
Tier-II Descriptive (English) 100 marks, 120 min – Essay 300 words (50), Grammar (30), Translation 25 words (20); up to 10× vacancies shortlisted for skill test
Tier-III Skill Test (qualifying) Typing test @ 40 wpm
Tier-IV Interview 15 marks, no minimum qualifying marks; final merit on Tier-II + Tier-IV combined

Process Server (Post Code 807/26)

Tier Format Marks / Detail
Tier-I Objective/MCQ (Bilingual, Eng+Hindi) 100 marks, 120 min (160 min for PwBD) – English (25), Hindi (25), GK (25), Arithmetic (25); up to 15× vacancies shortlisted
Tier-II Driving/Skill Test (qualifying) Conducted in real traffic conditions
Tier-III Interview 15 marks, no minimum qualifying marks; final selection on Tier-I + Tier-III combined

Peon/Orderly/Dak Peon (Post Code 808/26)

Tier Format Marks / Detail
Tier-I Objective/MCQ (Bilingual, Eng+Hindi) 100 marks, 120 min (160 min for PwBD) – English (25), Hindi (25), GK (25), Arithmetic (25); up to 10× vacancies shortlisted for interview
Tier-II Interview 15 marks, no minimum qualifying marks; final selection on Tier-I + Tier-II combined
  • DSSSB conducts the MCQ, Descriptive and Shorthand/Typing tests; Delhi District Courts (Tis Hazari) conducts the Driving Test/Interview and prepares the final merit list
  • Marks from Computer Based Examinations are normalized (where applicable) as per DSSSB's published formula
  • No re-evaluation/re-checking of answer sheets is permitted
  • In a tie, the senior-in-age candidate ranks higher; if DOB also matches, alphabetical order of first name (English) decides

How to Apply for DSSSB Combined Exam 2026

  1. Register (one-time) on dsssbonline.nic.in, if not already registered with DSSSB; this generates a common User ID/Password for all future DSSSB exams.
  2. Log in and apply online for the post(s)/post code(s) of your choice between 06.10.2026 (12:00 Noon) and 04.11.2026 (11:00 PM).
  3. Fill in all details carefully – no correction/modification (including category change) is allowed after final submission.
  4. Upload a recent, clear colour photograph (plain white/off-white background, full face, eyes open) and signature.
  5. Pay the applicable fee, if any, only through SBI e-Pay.
  6. Submit well before the closing date and take a printout of the confirmed application for your records.

Application Fee

Category Fee
UR / OBC / EWS (Male) ₹100
Women (any category) / SC / ST / PwBD / Ex-Servicemen Exempted (Nil)
Important: Ex-servicemen already re-employed on a regular basis in Central/Delhi Govt. civil posts after availing ESM reservation benefits are not eligible for the fee concession. Fee once paid is non-refundable, and only SBI e-Pay is accepted.

Documents Required

  • Matriculation/Secondary School certificate (date of birth proof)
  • Educational qualification certificates relevant to the post applied for (Graduation, Shorthand/Typing certificates, etc.)
  • LMV driving licence and proof of 2 years' driving experience (for Process Server)
  • OBC (Delhi) certificate with Non-Creamy-Layer certificate issued on/after 01.04.2026, where claiming OBC reservation (OBC-Outside-Delhi candidates are treated as UR)
  • EWS Income & Asset Certificate valid for FY 2026-27 (based on FY 2025-26 income), issued on or before 04.11.2026
  • Disability certificate, for PwBD candidates claiming reservation/relaxation (minimum 40% relevant disability required)
  • Discharge certificate/proof of military service, for Ex-Servicemen
  • Recent colour photograph (plain background) and signature, uploaded in the prescribed format
Supporting documents are sought only at the e-dossier stage after shortlisting; scrutiny is carried out by the concerned user department (Delhi District Courts), not DSSSB. Candidates who fail to upload the e-dossier within the given time are not considered further.

Important Conditions

  • Candidates must check their own eligibility (qualification, age, experience, PwBD suitability) for each post/department opted; ineligibility found at e-dossier/document verification leads to rejection for that post code with no reallocation
  • SC/ST/OBC/EWS/ESM/PwBD candidates selected purely on general merit are adjusted against unreserved vacancies, not reserved ones
  • Post/department preferences are exercised at the interview stage, are final and irreversible once confirmed, and cannot be changed later
  • Vacancies may vary (increase/decrease) at the discretion of the indenting department, with no compensation to candidates for such changes
  • Mobile phones, calculators, Bluetooth devices, smartwatches, and other electronic gadgets are strictly banned in the exam hall; possession leads to debarment and possible legal action
  • A prescribed dress code applies: light clothing with half sleeves, no big buttons/brooch/badge, Salwar/Trouser, and only slippers/low-heeled sandals (no shoes)
  • Only one registration and one application per candidate are allowed; multiple submissions lead to cancellation and debarment
  • In case of discrepancy between English, Hindi, Urdu and Punjabi versions of the advertisement, the English version prevails
  • DSSSB/Delhi District Courts reserve the right to change the examination scheme, cancel/modify the recruitment, or change exam centres at any stage

What Are State PSC Jobs?

State PSC jobs are government recruitment opportunities notified through State Public Service Commissions. These commissions recruit candidates for various posts and services under state government departments according to the rules applicable to each recruitment.

State PSC recruitment is not limited to State Civil Services examinations. Public Service Commissions may also recruit candidates for engineering, medical, teaching, agriculture, legal, scientific, technical, administrative and other departmental posts.

The posts available depend on vacancies reported by the respective state government departments and the recruitment notifications issued by the commission.

Popular Posts Recruited Through State PSCs

State Public Service Commissions recruit candidates for a wide range of government posts. Common recruitment categories may include:

  • State Civil Services
  • Administrative Services
  • Assistant Commissioner
  • Assistant Director
  • Assistant Professor
  • Lecturer
  • Medical Officer
  • Veterinary Officer
  • Assistant Engineer
  • Assistant Executive Engineer
  • Agriculture Officer
  • Food Safety Officer
  • Drug Inspector
  • Scientific Officer
  • Law Officer
  • Labour Officer
  • Revenue-related Posts
  • Technical Officers
  • Departmental Officers

The actual posts available vary by commission and recruitment notification.

PSC Jobs by Group (Group 1, 2, 2A, 4 & Others)

Several State Public Service Commissions including TNPSC, APPSC, and TSPSC classify recruitment into numbered "Groups" based on post seniority, pay scale, and administrative responsibility. Understanding these groups helps candidates identify which exam to prepare for based on their qualification and career goals.

Group Typical Posts Minimum Qualification Selection Stages
Group 1 Deputy Collector, DSP, Assistant Commissioner, District Registrar Bachelor's degree Prelims + Mains + Interview
Group 2 Assistant Section Officer, Tehsildar, Municipal Commissioner (Grade), Block Development Officer Bachelor's degree Prelims + Mains (some states include Interview)
Group 2A Junior Assistant, Bill Collector, Field Surveyor Bachelor's degree Written Exam (Certificate Verification)
Group 3 Various department Grade II/Non-Gazetted posts Varies by post Written Exam
Group 4 Junior Assistant, Typist, Steno-Typist, Bill Collector, Record Clerk, Village Administrative Officer (VAO) SSLC / 10th or 12th pass (varies by post) Single Written Exam (Certificate Verification)

Group numbering, post names, and minimum qualifications vary by state the table above reflects the common pattern used by TNPSC-style classification. Some states use different group labels or don't use numbered groups at all. Always confirm the exact group structure and eligibility on your state PSC's official notification.

Who Should Apply for Group 4?

Group 4 posts are typically entry-level government jobs open to candidates who have completed SSLC (10th) or Higher Secondary (12th), making them one of the most accessible and high-demand categories of PSC recruitment. These posts don't usually require a specific degree, have a single-stage written exam, and see some of the highest applicant volumes of any PSC exam due to the lower qualification bar and large number of annual vacancies.

State PSC Eligibility Criteria

There is no single eligibility rule for all State PSC jobs. Qualification, age limit, experience and other conditions differ depending on the commission and post.

Eligibility Criteria General Guidance
Educational Qualification Depends on the post and may include Diploma, Graduation, Engineering, Medicine, Law, Post Graduation or another prescribed qualification.
Age Limit Minimum and maximum age limits vary by commission and recruitment.
Age Relaxation Relaxation may be available to eligible categories according to the rules applicable to the recruitment.
State / Domicile Conditions State-specific eligibility, reservation, language or residency conditions may apply to certain recruitments.
Experience Some technical, teaching, specialist or senior posts require relevant professional experience.
Number of Attempts Attempt restrictions apply only where specifically prescribed for an examination or recruitment.

Important: Candidates should check the detailed recruitment notification before applying because eligibility conditions differ for every State PSC recruitment.

State PSC Selection Process

The State PSC selection process depends on the commission and the type of post. There is no single selection procedure followed for every PSC recruitment.

Depending on the recruitment, the selection process may include one or more of the following stages:

  • Preliminary Examination
  • Main Examination
  • Written Examination
  • Screening Test
  • Subject-specific Examination
  • Skill Test
  • Physical Test
  • Interview / Personality Test
  • Document Verification
  • Medical Examination

State Civil Services examinations may have Preliminary, Main and Interview stages, while technical, medical, teaching and departmental recruitment may follow a different selection process.

Always check the individual recruitment notification for the exact examination and selection procedure.

How to Apply for State PSC Jobs 2026

The application process differs slightly between commissions, but candidates can generally follow these steps:

  1. Find the required State PSC recruitment from the latest jobs table above.
  2. Open the detailed recruitment page.
  3. Check the post name, vacancies, qualification, age limit, application fee and important dates.
  4. Read the official recruitment notification carefully.
  5. Open the official application website or application link.
  6. Complete registration or One-Time Registration if required by the commission.
  7. Enter the required personal, educational and category details.
  8. Upload the prescribed photograph, signature and supporting documents.
  9. Pay the application fee if applicable.
  10. Review the application before final submission.
  11. Submit the application before the specified last date.
  12. Save or print the submitted application for future reference.

Candidates should submit applications only through the application method specified in the official notification.

State PSC Exam Pattern and Syllabus

There is no common exam pattern or syllabus for all State PSC recruitments.

State Civil Services examinations generally cover broader subjects such as General Studies and state-specific topics, while technical, medical, engineering, teaching and departmental recruitment may focus more heavily on subjects related to the post.

The following can differ between recruitments:

  • Number of papers
  • Objective or descriptive examination
  • Total marks
  • Exam duration
  • Negative marking
  • Minimum qualifying marks
  • Language requirements
  • Subject-specific syllabus
  • Interview or skill test requirements

Candidates should refer to the syllabus and exam pattern issued for the specific State PSC recruitment they are applying for.

State PSC Jobs vs UPSC Jobs

State Public Service Commissions and the Union Public Service Commission conduct different recruitment processes.

State PSC UPSC
Conducts recruitment for posts and services connected with the respective state. Conducts recruitment and examinations for various Union Government and All India Services posts.
Recruitment rules differ from one State PSC to another. Recruitment is conducted under the rules applicable to UPSC examinations and vacancies.
May recruit for State Civil Services, engineering, medical, teaching, technical and departmental posts. Conducts Civil Services Examination and various other recruitment examinations for Union Government posts.

Candidates looking for Union Government recruitment through UPSC can visit the UPSC Jobs page.

PSC vs PCS - What Is the Difference?

PSC stands for Public Service Commission. It refers to the constitutional commission responsible for conducting recruitment for various government posts and services within its jurisdiction.

PCS commonly refers to Provincial Civil Service or State Civil Services posts and examinations.

A State Public Service Commission may conduct a State Civil Services or PCS examination, but it can also conduct recruitment for many other positions such as Medical Officer, Assistant Engineer, Lecturer, Agriculture Officer and departmental posts.

Therefore, State PSC Jobs covers a broader range of recruitment than only PCS or State Civil Services examinations.

How to Choose the Right State PSC Recruitment

Before applying for a State PSC vacancy, candidates should compare the recruitment requirements with their qualification and preferences.

Check the following details:

  • Required educational qualification
  • Age limit
  • Category and reservation conditions
  • State or language requirements, if any
  • Number of vacancies
  • Pay scale or salary
  • Job location
  • Application fee
  • Selection process
  • Examination pattern
  • Application deadline

Apply only after confirming that you meet the eligibility conditions mentioned in the official recruitment notification.

State PSC Recruitment Updates You Should Check

A recruitment notification can sometimes be followed by additional notices from the commission. Candidates should continue checking recruitment updates even after submitting their application.

Important updates may include:

  • Application date extension
  • Correction window
  • Vacancy revision
  • Exam date
  • Exam city information
  • Admit card
  • Answer key
  • Result
  • Interview schedule
  • Document verification schedule
  • Final selection result

Relevant updates should be linked from the individual recruitment page whenever they are released.

Why Check State PSC Jobs on OnlyJobs?

OnlyJobs brings State Public Service Commission recruitment information together in one place so candidates can quickly find current opportunities without checking multiple commission websites individually.

For each recruitment, candidates can find important details such as:

  • Recruiting commission
  • Post name
  • Total vacancies
  • Educational qualification
  • Age limit
  • Salary or pay scale
  • Application fee
  • Selection process
  • Application dates
  • Official notification
  • Official application link

Recruitment information should be checked against the official State Public Service Commission notification before publication. Important corrections, vacancy revisions and date extensions should also be updated whenever they are released.

Latest State PSC Notifications - Frequently Asked Questions

What are State PSC Jobs?

State PSC Jobs are government recruitment opportunities notified through State Public Service Commissions for various posts and services under state government departments.

Which State PSC jobs are currently open?

Currently open recruitments are listed in the Latest State PSC Jobs 2026 table at the top of this page. The list is updated when new recruitment notifications and application updates are released.

Where can I find the latest State PSC recruitment notifications?

You can check the latest State PSC recruitment notifications on this page or select your commission from the State-wise PSC Jobs section to find recruitment specific to your state.

What qualification is required for State PSC jobs?

There is no single qualification required for all State PSC jobs. Depending on the post, candidates may need a Diploma, Graduation, Engineering degree, Medical qualification, Law degree, Post Graduation or another specified qualification.

Are all State PSC jobs for graduates?

No. Eligibility depends on the individual recruitment. Many administrative posts require a degree, while technical, professional and departmental posts may have different qualification requirements.

What is the age limit for State PSC jobs?

The minimum and maximum age limits vary according to the commission and post. Candidates should check the age criteria given in the individual recruitment notification.

Is age relaxation available for State PSC recruitment?

Age relaxation may be available to eligible categories according to the rules applicable to the respective recruitment. The exact relaxation should be checked in the official notification.

Is domicile compulsory for State PSC jobs?

Not for every State PSC recruitment. Some vacancies may have state-specific residency, reservation, language or other eligibility requirements. Candidates should check the relevant recruitment rules before applying.

What is the selection process for State PSC jobs?

The selection process varies by post. It may include a Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, written test, screening test, skill test, interview, physical test, document verification or medical examination.

Do all State PSC recruitments have Prelims and Mains?

No. Prelims and Mains are common in some State Civil Services examinations, but many technical, medical, teaching and departmental recruitments follow a different examination or selection process.

How can I apply for State PSC recruitment?

Open the required recruitment from the latest jobs table, read the eligibility and application details, check the official notification and use the official application link provided on the recruitment page.

What is the difference between State PSC and UPSC?

State PSCs conduct recruitment mainly for posts and services connected with their respective states, while UPSC conducts recruitment and examinations for various Union Government and All India Services posts.

Is PSC the same as PCS?

No. PSC means Public Service Commission, while PCS generally refers to Provincial Civil Service or State Civil Services. A State PSC can recruit for PCS as well as many other administrative, technical, medical and departmental posts.

Where can I check State PSC admit cards?

When an admit card is released, the related recruitment page should be updated with the admit card information and official download link. Candidates can also check the OnlyJobs Admit Card section.

Where can I check State PSC results?

State PSC result updates can be checked through the individual recruitment page or the OnlyJobs Results section.

How often is this State PSC Jobs page updated?

The page is updated when new State PSC recruitment notifications, application extensions and other important recruitment updates become available.

What Is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job is any government job opportunity offered across India's central and state government departments - spanning all 28 states and 8 union territories. The term "Bharat" simply emphasises pan-India coverage: a Bharat Sarkari Job notification could originate from a central body like the SSC, UPSC, or Indian Railways, or from a state public service commission recruiting for state-level posts. Regardless of origin, these roles share the defining traits Indian aspirants seek - long-term job security, government pay scales, and statutory retirement benefits.

Sarkari Job vs Private Job

A sarkari job differs from private-sector employment in a few important ways: government positions are governed by service rules that protect against arbitrary termination, salaries follow Pay Commission recommendations rather than market negotiation, and employees are entitled to pension schemes (NPS or OPS depending on recruitment year), medical coverage under CGHS, and fixed working hours. Private jobs, by contrast, often offer higher starting pay in competitive fields but carry less structural job security.

Railway Jobs (RRB NTPC, ALP, Group D)

Indian Railways is the country's largest single recruiter, with RRB NTPC, Group D, ALP, JE, and Technician posts opening in large batches. Check live Railway vacancies on our Railway Jobs hub.

Defence Jobs (Army, Navy, Air Force)

Defence recruitment covers Indian Army (including Agniveer), Navy, Air Force, BSF, CRPF, CISF, and ITBP postings. See ongoing openings on our Defence Jobs hub.

Teaching Jobs (KVS, NVS, State Boards)

Teaching sarkari jobs include KVS, NVS, DSSSB, and state education board recruitment for TGT, PGT, and PRT posts. Explore current teaching vacancies on our Teaching Jobs hub.

SSC & UPSC Notifications

SSC (CGL, CHSL, MTS, GD) and UPSC (Civil Services, CDS, NDA) notifications remain the most closely tracked central-government exams. Full notification archives are available on our SSC Jobs and UPSC Jobs hubs.
