सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

Documents Required for Sarkari Form

Typical documents needed: recent passport-size photograph (as per specified size/format), scanned signature, educational certificates and mark sheets, category certificate (if applicable), and a valid ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN).

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

  • Submitting a photo or signature that doesn't match the specified pixel/size requirements.
  • Missing the last date due to server load - apply at least 2–3 days before deadline.
  • Entering a name or date of birth that doesn't match your certificates exactly.
  • Forgetting to download and save the final submitted form and payment receipt.

सबसे पहले संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना पढ़ें, पात्रता जांचें, फिर वैध ईमेल और मोबाइल नंबर से रजिस्ट्रेशन करके फॉर्म भरें, दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें और आवेदन शुल्क जमा करें।

Is OnlyJobs reliable for sarkarijob updates?

Yes - OnlyJobs has tracked sarkarijob notifications since 2011, cross-verifying every listing against official department websites before publishing.

What is the difference between a Sarkari Job and a private-sector job?

Sarkari jobs offer government-backed job security, pension (NPS/OPS), fixed working hours, and statutory benefits, while private jobs typically offer market-driven pay with fewer long-term security guarantees.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Forest Department Posts List

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Forest Guard / Forest Watcher / Field Guard: 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board
  • Forester: 12th pass, often with Science subjects; some states require a diploma in Forestry
  • Range Forest Officer: Graduate degree, frequently in Science, Agriculture, or Forestry
  • ACF / IFS: Graduate degree in a relevant discipline (Botany, Zoology, Forestry, Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Engineering, or Environmental Science), followed by the respective state or UPSC exam

Age Limit & Relaxation

The general age limit for Forest Guard and Forester posts is usually 18–27 years, though this varies by state. Age relaxation is generally available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD candidates, and other reserved categories as per government norms.

Reservation & Age Relaxation for Ex-Servicemen

Most state forest departments reserve a fixed percentage of Forest Guard, Forester, and Beat Guard posts for ex-servicemen, in addition to SC, ST, OBC, and EWS reservations. Candidates applying for jobs for ex servicemen in forest department typically receive:

  • Additional age relaxation, usually 3–5 years beyond the general age cap (or as per length of military service)
  • Relaxed physical standards in several states
  • A reserved vacancy quota, separate from the general merit list

Exact quota percentages and relaxation norms differ by state, so always cross-check the specific notification before applying.

Physical Standards

Most Forest Guard and Forester posts require candidates to clear height, chest measurement (for male candidates), and a Physical Efficiency Test involving running, walking, or trekking - since the job involves regular field patrol duty in forest terrain.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern for Forest Officer & Forest Guard Posts

The selection process for forest department recruitment generally involves multiple stages, designed to test both academic knowledge and physical fitness given the field nature of the job.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  1. Written Examination - objective-type questions on General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, Mathematics, and sometimes Forestry/Environment-related topics
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) / Physical Standard Test (PST) - running, walking/trekking distance, height and chest measurement
  3. Document Verification - verification of educational certificates, age proof, category certificates, and (where applicable) ex-servicemen discharge documents
  4. Medical Examination - fitness check before final appointment
  5. Final Merit List - based on combined written exam and PET/PST scores, as per each state's weightage formula

  • Basic Mathematics / Numerical Ability

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

  2. Open the official notification and read the eligibility, fee, and important dates.
  3. Register on the recruiter's official portal.
  4. Fill in the application with your LLB/LLM, Bar enrolment, and personal details.
  5. Upload the required documents and photograph.
  6. Pay the application fee (if any) and submit before the last date.
  7. Save or print the confirmation for future reference.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

What is OnlyJobs?

OnlyJobs is the common Hindi-English term for the outcome of any Indian government recruitment or board examination - the published result, merit list, or scorecard that tells a candidate whether they have qualified. Around this single moment sits an entire cycle: the recruitment notification, the online application form, the admit card (hall ticket), the exam, the answer key, the cut-off marks, and finally the result and document verification. When people search for a OnlyJobs, सरकारी रिजल्ट, or a OnlyJobs result, they are usually looking for one trusted place that tracks every one of these stages without sending them to dozens of separate official portals.

OnlyJobs has done exactly that since 2011. This page brings together the latest OnlyJobs results, admit cards, answer keys, and online-form notifications from national bodies such as SSC, UPSC, the Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB), and banking recruiters like IBPS and SBI, alongside every State Public Service Commission across India's 28 states and 8 union territories. How to Check Your OnlyJobs 2026 Online (Step-by-Step)

Checking a OnlyJobs result takes only a few minutes once you know the steps:

  • Find your exam in the Latest Results section below, or use the search bar to type the exam name (e.g., "SSC CGL" or "RRB NTPC").
  • Read the result summary to confirm the post, organisation, and result date.
  • Open the official portal link provided in the article (e.g., ssc.nic.in, upsc.gov.in).
  • Enter your Roll Number or Registration ID along with your date of birth, as required by that exam body.
  • Download or screenshot your result/scorecard for future reference - most government portals remove results after a few weeks.
  • Check the next stage (cut-off, document verification, interview call letter) - OnlyJobs lists this under the same exam tag so you can track the full recruitment cycle.

Note: If the official server is busy on result day, wait a few minutes and try again rather than refreshing repeatedly; heavy traffic is normal in the first hour after a major result is declared.

What is OnlyJobs?

"OnlyJobs" generally refers to the final outcome of a government recruitment (selection lists, scorecards), while "OnlyJobs Result" can also include preliminary/stage-wise outcomes like Prelims or Tier-1 results. OnlyJobs covers both under each exam's dedicated page.

Canara Bank Graduate Apprentice Notification 2026 has been released on the official website. A total of 3500 vacancies have been announced through the Canara Bank Graduate Apprentice Recruitment 2026.

Candidates aged between 20 and 28 years who have a Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a university recognized by the Government of India, passed not earlier than 01.01.2023 and not later than 01.09.2026 are eligible to apply for these Graduate Apprentice vacancies. The online application process for Canara Bank Graduate Apprentice Recruitment 2026 will remain open until 17-10-2026.

Candidates can download the official notification PDF and apply online through the direct links provided below in this article.

Canara Bank Graduate Apprentice Vacancy 2026 Notification PDF

Candidates who are interested in applying for the Canara Bank Recruitment 2026 should first download and carefully read the official notification PDF. The notification contains complete details about vacancy distribution, eligibility criteria, age limit, stipend/ salary, selection process, important dates, and application instructions. Reading the official document is important to ensure that you meet all requirements before submitting the application form.

  • Download Canara Bank Graduate Apprentice Job 2026 Notification PDF
  • Apply Online
  • Official Website

Canara Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026 Overview

Canara Bank has published the advertisement "Engagement of Graduate Apprentices under Apprentices Act, 1961 for FY 2026-27". Candidates must first register on the apprenticeship portal and then apply through the Bank's website.

Head Office Bengaluru
Recruitment Name Engagement of Graduate Apprentices under Apprentices Act, 1961 for FY 2026-27
Post Name Graduate Apprentice
Number of Training Seats 3500 (provisional; may vary according to the actual requirement of the Bank)
Notification Date 25.09.2026
Application Mode Online
Application Dates 01.10.2026 to 17.10.2026 (both days inclusive)
Qualification Degree (Graduation) in any discipline
Age Limit Minimum 20 years, maximum 28 years as on 01.09.2026
Period of Apprenticeship Training 12 Months
Stipend Rs. 16,650 per month (including subsidy amount, if any, by Govt. of India)
Application Fee SC/ ST/ PwBD: NIL; All Others: Rs. 500 (incl. intimation charges)
Selection Basis State-wise merit list based on 12th Std (HSC/ 10+2)/ Diploma marks, followed by document verification
Official Websites www.canarabank.bank.in and https:/ / nats.education.gov.in

Canara Bank Apprentice Important Dates

The online registration window is short, so candidates who have not yet registered on the NATS portal should do so first.

The dates for document verification and the local language test are not specified in the notification. Further announcements will be published only on the Bank's website.

Canara Bank Apprentice Vacancy 2026

Canara Bank has announced 3500 training seats across states and Union Territories. Candidates can opt for training seats in only one state. The seats are provisional and may vary according to the actual requirement of the Bank.

Important Points About Training Seats

  • Candidates can opt for training seats in only ONE STATE under this project.
  • Candidates will be able to give their order of preference for all districts in the selected state. Allotment will be need based and subject to availability of training seats in the respective districts.
  • The Bank reserves the right to allot a training seat in any district of the selected state as per administrative requirement.
  • Candidates should ensure they fulfil the eligibility criteria as on the date of eligibility before applying.
  • Candidates should check the Bank's website (www.canarabank.bank.in, Careers, Recruitment, Engagement of Graduate Apprentices in Canara Bank under Apprentices Act, 1961 for FY 2026-27) for details and updates.

Canara Bank Apprentice Eligibility Criteria

All eligibility conditions, including age and qualification, are computed as on 01.09.2026 (inclusive). The tables below summarise the main conditions.

Canara Bank Apprentice Qualification

 
Educational Qualification A Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a university recognized by the Govt. of India, or any equivalent qualification recognized as such by the Central Government.
Graduation Passing Window Candidates must have passed their Graduation not earlier than 01.01.2023 and not later than 01.09.2026 (both days inclusive).
Test of Local Language Candidates who produce a 10th or 12th standard mark sheet/ certificate showing they studied the opted local language will not have to take the local language test. For other candidates, the test will be conducted when they are called for Document Verification. Candidates who fail to qualify will not be engaged as apprentices.
Physical/ Medical Fitness Engagement is subject to the candidate being declared medically fit as per the requirement of the Bank.
Portal Registration Candidates need a 100% complete profile on https:/ / nats.education.gov.in before applying.

Canara Bank Apprentice Age Limit

The age limit is a minimum of 20 years and a maximum of 28 years as on 01.09.2026. Candidates must have been born not earlier than 02.09.1998 and not later than 01.09.2006 (both days inclusive). The maximum age limit applies to General Category and EWS candidates.

 
Sl. No. Category Age Relaxation
1 Scheduled Caste/ Scheduled Tribe 5 years
2 Other Backward Classes (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
3 Persons with Benchmark Disabilities as defined under "The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016" 10 years
4 Widows, divorced women and women legally separated from their husbands who have not remarried Age concession up to the age of 35 years for General/ EWS, 38 years for OBC and 40 years for SC/ ST candidates

Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying.

Other Eligibility Conditions and Notes

  1. Age relaxation for SC/ ST/ OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates is allowed on a cumulative basis with only one of the remaining categories for which age relaxation is permitted.
  2. Candidates seeking age relaxation must submit the necessary certificate(s) in original along with photocopies at the time of document verification/ reporting for On-the-Job training and at any later stage required by the Bank.
  3. Reservation for PwBD is horizontal and within the overall training vacancies for the State.
  4. No Ex-servicemen/ Disabled Ex-Servicemen shall be engaged as an apprentice, and there is no reservation for them in this engagement.
  5. The candidate should not have undergone Apprenticeship Training with Canara Bank or any other organization earlier, should not be pursuing Apprenticeship Training under the Apprentices Act 1961, and should not have been terminated during Apprenticeship Training due to their own fault.
  6. Candidates who have undergone training or have job experience of one or more years after completing their educational qualification are not eligible.
  7. SC/ ST/ OBC/ PwBD candidates need a Caste/ Category Certificate issued by a competent authority in the format prescribed by the Government of India.
  8. OBC candidates need a valid OBC certificate with a non-creamy layer clause. OBC candidates who come under the creamy layer are not entitled to OBC reservation and should indicate their category as General in the online application.

Canara Bank Apprentice Reservation Details

Reservation for SC/ ST/ OBC/ EWS/ PwBD candidates is as per the prescribed reservation percentages of the respective States/ UTs as per Government guidelines. Candidates from reserved categories, including those for whom no reservation is mentioned, may apply for unreserved vacancies if they fulfil all eligibility conditions applicable to the unreserved category.

PwBD Reservation

Under section 34 of "The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016", persons with benchmark disabilities are eligible for reservation. The post is identified as suitable for the following disability categories as defined in the Schedule of the RPwD Act 2016.

  • Visual Impairment (VI): Persons with blindness (total absence of sight; visual acuity less than 3/ 60 or less than 10/ 200 (Snellen) in the better eye with best possible correction; or limitation of the field of vision subtending an angle of less than 10 degrees) or low vision (visual acuity not exceeding 6/ 18 or less than 20/ 60 up to 3/ 60 or up to 10/ 200 (Snellen) in the better eye with best possible correction; or limitation of the field of vision subtending an angle of less than 40 degrees up to 10 degrees).
  • Hearing Impaired (HI): Deaf (70 DB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears) or Hard of Hearing (60 DB to 70 DB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears).
  • Orthopedically Challenged/ Locomotor Disability (OC/ LD): Inability to execute distinctive activities associated with movement of self and objects resulting from affliction of the musculoskeletal or nervous system or both, including Cerebral Palsy, Leprosy Cured, Dwarfism (adult height of 4 feet 10 inches (147 centimeters) or less), Muscular Dystrophy, Acid Attack Victims, Spinal Deformity and Spinal Injury without any associated neurological/ limb dysfunction.
  • Intellectual Disability (ID): Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Specific Learning Disability (SLD) and Mental Illness (MI), as defined in the notification.
  • Multiple Disabilities: Multiple disabilities among the categories above.

Only persons with benchmark disabilities are eligible for reservation. A benchmark disability means not less than 40% of a specified disability, as certified by the certifying authority. Candidates must submit a disability certificate issued by a Competent Authority as per Government of India guidelines, which is subject to verification or re-verification at any point. PwBD reservation is not applicable on the basis of a temporary disability certificate. It is only for persons with irreversible permanent benchmark disability in terms of O.M. No. 36035/ 8/ 2023-Estt. (Res-II) dated 19.05.2023 of DoPT. Government guidelines may change from time to time.

EWS Reservation

  • Persons not covered under the reservation schemes for SC, ST and OBC, and whose family gross annual income is below Rs. 8.00 lakh, are identified as EWS. Income includes all sources (salary, agriculture, business, profession, etc.) for the financial year prior to the year of application.
  • Families owning any of these assets are excluded irrespective of income: 5 acres of agricultural land and above; a residential flat of 1000 sq. ft. and above; a residential plot of 100 sq. yards and above in notified municipalities; a residential plot of 200 sq. yards and above in areas other than notified municipalities.
  • Property held in different locations or cities is clubbed for the land or property holding test.
  • The EWS benefit requires an Income and Asset Certificate issued by a Competent Authority in the format prescribed by the Government of India. Shortlisted candidates must bring it at document verification.
  • "Family" includes the candidate, parents and siblings below 18 years, and the spouse and children below 18 years.

Disclaimer in the notification: EWS vacancies are tentative and subject to further directives of the Government of India and the outcome of any litigation.

Canara Bank Apprentice Stipend and Salary

Apprentices are not employees of Canara Bank. A monthly stipend is paid instead of a salary during the apprenticeship period.

 
Monthly Stipend Rs. 16,650 (including subsidy amount, if any, by Govt. of India)
Paid by Canara Bank Rs. 10,500 per month into the apprentice's account
Government Share Rs. 6,150, credited directly to the apprentice's bank account through DBT mode as per extant guidelines
Deductions Stipend is paid each month after adjusting loss of pay, if any
Other Allowances/ Benefits Not eligible for any other allowances or benefits

Canara Bank Apprentice Application Fee

The fee is non-refundable and includes GST. It is payable online only.

 
Category Application Fee / Intimation Charges (Non-Refundable)
SC/ ST/ PwBD NIL
All Others Rs. 500 (incl. intimation charges)

Payment can be made by Debit Cards (RuPay/ Visa/ MasterCard/ Maestro), Credit Cards, Internet Banking, IMPS, Cash Cards or Mobile Wallets. An e-receipt is generated after a successful transaction. Candidates should not press Back or Refresh after submitting payment information, to avoid double charge.

Canara Bank Apprentice Selection Process

Selection is merit-based. The notification does not describe a written examination.

  1. Merit list: Prepared state-wise in descending order of marks/ percentage in 12th Std (HSC/ 10+2)/ Diploma Examination. Ties are ranked by age in descending order.
  2. Minimum marks: Not less than 60% (55% for SC/ ST/ PwBD) in 12th Std/ Diploma. Fractions are ignored, so 59.99% is treated as below 60% and 54.99% as below 55%.
  3. Document Verification and local language test: Conducted during the Document Verification process. Original documents are checked. Any discrepancy leads to summary disqualification.
  4. Final selection is subject to verification of eligibility and application information, qualification in the local language test of the opted State where applicable, and being declared medically fit.

Where CGPA/ OGPA is awarded, it must be converted into percentage in the online application, with a certificate from the appropriate authority stating the conversion norms. Percentage is total marks obtained in all subjects in all semesters/ years divided by aggregate maximum marks, multiplied by 100. The merit list is prepared only on the information submitted in the online application.

How to Apply for Canara Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Candidates must apply online. No other mode of application will be accepted.

Canara Bank Apprentice Apply Online

  1. Register on https:/ / nats.education.gov.in and complete your profile to 100%. Keep the enrollment number generated.
  2. Visit www.canarabank.bank.in, open Careers, then Recruitment, then the link "Engagement of Graduate Apprentices in Canara Bank under Apprentices Act, 1961 for FY 2026-27".
  3. Click "CLICK HERE FOR NEW REGISTRATION" and enter basic information. A provisional registration number and password are generated and sent by email and SMS. Saved data can be reopened using them.
  4. Enter the NATS enrollment ID, fill all fields, and choose one State along with district preferences.
  5. Upload the photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration as specified below.
  6. Use "SAVE AND NEXT" to verify details. No change is possible after clicking FINAL SUBMIT.
  7. Pay the fee online (if applicable), then take a printout of the application and e-receipt.

Apply well before the closing date to avoid website load issues. Only one application should be submitted; if multiple are submitted, only the latest valid completed application is retained.

Documents Required to Apply Online

Signature 140 x 60 pixels 10 KB to 20 KB Black ink on white paper; CAPITAL LETTERS not accepted
Left thumb impression 240 x 240 pixels at 200 DPI (3cm x 3cm) 20 KB to 50 KB jpg/ jpeg; black or blue ink on white paper
Handwritten declaration 800 x 400 pixels at 200 DPI (10cm x 5cm) 50 KB to 100 KB jpg/ jpeg; English, black ink, own handwriting, not in CAPITAL LETTERS

The declaration text is: "I, ____ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required." Candidates who cannot write may type the declaration and put their left thumb impression below it. Images should be scanned at a minimum of 200 dpi in true colour, in JPG/ JPEG format. Unclear or smudged images may lead to rejection.

Candidates also need a valid personal email ID and mobile number, active until the process ends, and should spell their name as in the SSC/ SSLC/ X Standard marks card (or as per Gazette Notification/ Marriage Certificate if changed). An application that is incomplete or has unsuccessful fee payment is invalid. If no email/ SMS intimation is received, the application is considered not successfully registered.

Documents to Be Produced at the Time of Engagement

Originals with a self-attested photocopy must be submitted, failing which the candidate may not be permitted to join.

  • Valid system-generated printout of the online application.
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate from a Competent Authority or SSLC/ Std. X Certificate with date of birth).
  • Photo ID: Passport, Aadhar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, Driving License or any other photo ID issued by Statutory Authorities.
  • Mark sheets/ certificates from SSC onwards to the highest examination passed, including semester/ year-wise mark sheets and the final degree, with proper Board/ University proof that the result was declared on or before the cut-off date.
  • Income and Asset Certificate in the prescribed format (EWS candidates).
  • Caste Certificate in the prescribed format (SC/ ST/ OBC). For OBC, the certificate must include the non-creamy layer clause, be valid as on the date of notification, and the caste name must tally letter by letter with the Government list.
  • UDID card and Disability Certificate from a Medical Board (at least three members, including a specialist) in the prescribed format (PwBD candidates).
  • Any other relevant documents in support of eligibility.

The application fee and intimation charges (non-refundable) are ₹750 for UR/EWS/OBC candidates; there is no fee for SC/ST/PwBD candidates. SBI SCO Selection Process

  • Shortlisting: mere fulfilment of minimum qualification and experience does not entitle a candidate to be called for interview; the shortlisting committee decides the parameters and number of candidates called.
  • Interview: one or more rounds of personal, telephonic, or video interview, carrying 100 marks; the qualifying marks are decided by the Bank.
  • CTC Negotiation: conducted individually with shortlisted candidates, at the time of interview or after completion of the interview process.
  • Merit List: prepared in descending order based on interview scores only; candidates tied at the cut-off mark are ranked by age, in descending order.

  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel the recruitment process entirely, or for any particular post, at any stage without assigning reasons.
  • Any legal proceedings arising from this recruitment fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of courts at Mumbai.

Under Project No. 2026-27/02 dated 01.08.2026, BOI is inviting applications for 205 vacancies across 48 distinct posts ranging from Officer (Scale I) to Chief Manager (Scale IV). Candidates with qualifications in Computer Science/IT, Law, Fire Engineering, and Civil Engineering can apply online between 10.09.2026 and 05.10.2026.

In brief: BOI is recruiting for IT and specialist officer roles spanning Full-Stack Engineering, Digital Platforms, Information Security, DevSecOps, Data Engineering, Database Administration, Law Officer, Fire Officer, Security Officer, and Civil Engineer, among others. Eligible Indian citizens (and other nationalities specified in the notice) meeting the post-specific qualification and experience criteria as on 01.08.2026 can apply online through the official BOI website. The application mode is online only, and postings will be anywhere in India.

Bank of India Recruitment 2026 Age Limit

Minimum and maximum age are calculated as on 01.08.2026 and vary by post - from 21-30 years for Scale I Officer posts up to 28-42 years for Scale IV Chief Manager posts. Upper age relaxation is available as follows: SC/ST – 5 years; OBC (non-creamy layer) – 3 years; PwBD – 10 years; Ex-Servicemen/ECOs/SSCOs – 5 years; persons affected by 1984 riots – 5 years.

BOI Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

  • Online Examination: English Language (25 marks, qualifying only) + Professional Knowledge relevant to the post (100 marks), composite duration 100 minutes
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 35% for General/EWS (30% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD)
  • Personal Interview: Maximum 100 marks; qualifying 50% for General/EWS, 45% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD; candidates called at approximately 1:3 ratio to vacancies
  • Final weightage: Online Examination and Interview combined at 60:40
  • Bank may, at its discretion, select solely through Interview without an online exam

  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC-Non-Creamy Layer/EWS/PWD), as applicable
  • Experience certificates and mandatory certification proofs relevant to the post applied for
  • No Objection Certificate (for candidates in government/PSU employment)

How to Apply for Bank of India Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official website www.bankofindia.bank.in and click on 'CAREER'
  2. Click the link "Recruitment of Officers in various streams upto Scale IV – Project No. 2026-27/02 Notice dated 01.08.2026"
  3. Click 'APPLY ONLINE' and complete new registration to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password
  4. Fill in personal, educational, and experience details; upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and hand-written declaration as per specifications
  5. Preview and verify all details before clicking 'COMPLETE REGISTRATION'
  6. Pay the application fee/intimation charges online
  7. Take a printout of the system-generated application form and e-receipt for personal record

Important Instructions

  • Candidates can apply for only one post; multiple applications will retain only the latest valid one
  • Candidates already holding a similar post in Bank of India in the past are not eligible
  • No change of category or other application details is permitted after registration
  • Selected candidates must deposit a refundable security deposit: ₹1,00,000 (JMGS-I), ₹2,00,000 (MMGS-II), ₹3,00,000 (MMGS-III and above)
  • All mandatory certifications must be valid as on 01.08.2026
  • Bank reserves the right to change, cancel, or modify vacancies, posts, or the selection process at any stage

  3. Select "Recruitment Process for Probationary Officer CRP PO/MT CRP-XVI".
  4. Click on "Download Online Main Exam Call Letter for CRP PO/MT CRP-XVI".
  5. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Date of Birth/Password, then fill in the captcha code.
  6. Your IBPS PO Mains Admit Card 2026 will be displayed on the screen.
  7. Check your exam date, centre details, reporting time, and personal information carefully.
  8. Download and take at least 2-3 printouts of the call letter for the exam day and future reference.

Also Read: WBP Constable Final Result 2026

Forgot Registration Number or Password?

If you have misplaced your registration number or password, you can retrieve it using the steps below:

  1. Visit the official website, ibps.in.
  2. On the login page, click on the PO/MT examination admit card link.
  3. Click on the "Forgot Password?" button.
  4. Enter your registration number along with your registered mobile number or email ID.
  5. Click submit a new password will be sent to your registered email.

Important Instructions for the IBPS PO Mains Exam

Candidates must follow these exam-day guidelines carefully:

  • Carry a printed copy of the IBPS PO Mains Admit Card along with an original valid photo ID proof.
  • Reach the exam centre at least 30 to 45 minutes before the reporting time mentioned on the call letter.
  • Carry 2 to 3 passport-size photographs identical to the one uploaded on the call letter.
  • Electronic devices, smartwatches, calculators, Bluetooth devices, and study materials are not allowed inside the exam hall.
  • Biometric verification will be conducted at the exam centre to maintain the integrity of the process.
  • Ensure the photograph and signature printed on the admit card are clear and legible.
  • Scribe-related documents are required only for candidates using a registered scribe under PwBD guidelines.

Documents Required for the IBPS PO Mains Exam

Candidates must carry the following mandatory documents to the exam centre:

  • Printed IBPS PO Mains Call Letter / Admit Card
  • Original photo identity proof (Aadhaar Card/e-Aadhaar, PAN Card, Voter ID, Driving Licence, or Passport), along with a photocopy
  • 2 to 3 extra passport-size photographs matching the one on the call letter
  • Scribe-related documents, only if applicable

Also Read: UP Police PET Admit Card 2026

Details Mentioned on the IBPS PO Mains Admit Card

Once downloaded, candidates should verify the following details printed on the call letter and report any discrepancy to IBPS immediately:

  • Candidate's Name, Photograph, and Signature
  • Father's/Mother's or Husband's Name
  • Date of Birth, Gender, and Category
  • Roll Number/User ID and Registration Number
  • Post Applied (CRP PO/MT CRP-XVI)
  • Exam Date, Stage, and Shift Timing
  • Name, Code, and Complete Address of the Exam Centre
  • Reporting Time and Gate-Closing Instructions
  • Space for candidate's signature and left thumb impression
  • Exam-day rules and instructions

What to Do in Case of an Error on the Admit Card?

If you notice any mistake or discrepancy on your IBPS PO Mains Admit Card, follow these steps:

  1. Verify your name spelling, date of birth, registration number, and category carefully.
  2. Check whether your photograph and signature are clearly visible.
  3. Confirm the centre name, shift timing, and full address are correct.
  4. Contact the IBPS helpdesk through the official support email or helpline number given on the portal.
  5. Keep your online application form and registration acknowledgement ready for faster resolution.
  6. Download the corrected admit card once the issue has been updated by IBPS.

IBPS PO Mains Exam Date and Pattern 2026

The IBPS PO Mains exam will be held on 4 October 2026. It is a Computer-Based Test that evaluates candidates on Reasoning & Computer Aptitude, General/Economy/Banking Awareness, English Language, and Data Analysis & Interpretation, along with a descriptive English Language Writing Test (Essay & Letter). Negative marking applies for wrong answers in the objective sections. Exact sectional timings, marks distribution, and negative-marking ratio are not available in the source material used for this article and should be checked on the admit card and the official notification.

What After RBI Assistant Mains Result 2026?

Candidates shortlisted in the Mains Result must now appear for the Language Proficiency Test (LPT), the final stage of the RBI Assistant selection process. The LPT tests a candidate's ability to read, write, speak, and understand the official/local language of the RBI office for which they applied. Candidates who studied the relevant local language up to the 10th or 12th standard are generally exempted; others must appear for and clear the LPT to remain in contention for final selection. The LPT is qualifying in nature no marks from it are added to the final merit list, but clearing it is mandatory. RBI is yet to announce the exact LPT schedule, venue, and reporting-time details for this cycle; candidates should watch the official portal for this notification.

Exim Bank Deputy Manager & Manager Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility (age, educational qualification, etc.) is computed as on 31-08-2026, as detailed below for each post.

Manager (Grade/Scale MM II) – Internal Audit (2 Posts)

Qualification: Minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA in Graduation (minimum 3-year full-time course), AND Post Graduation (MBA / PGDBA / PGDBM / MMS) with specialization in Finance / International Business / Foreign Trade, or Chartered Accountant (CA). The Post Graduation course should be a minimum 2-year full-time duration with a specialization in Finance and minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA. For CA, passing the professional examination is sufficient, and membership of ICAI is mandatory.

Experience: Minimum 3 years of experience in a scheduled commercial bank, an all-India financial institution, or another organization of repute, in internal audit / credit audit, including handling preparation and submission of reports by internal/concurrent auditors, audit compliance, analysis and timely submission of audit observations to the audit committee, review of internal/concurrent audit scope and systems/procedures/controls, and experience dealing with RBI on audit/inspection matters (in Scale I or equivalent).

Deputy Manager (Grade/Scale JM I) – Banking Operations (6 Posts)

Qualification: Minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA in Graduation (minimum 3-year full-time course), AND Post Graduation (MBA / PGDBA / PGDBM / MMS) with specialization in Finance / International Business / Foreign Trade, or Chartered Accountant (CA), on the same terms as above.

Experience (as on 31-08-2026): Minimum 1 year of post-qualification (Post Graduation or CA) work experience in a reputed commercial bank / financial institution / state level term lending institution, with skills in project finance, credit appraisal, term lending, analysis of cross-border risks, and financing of overseas joint ventures.

Final selection is based on combined performance in the Written Examination (out of 100, with 70% weightage) and the Interview (out of 100, with 30% weightage). A pre-recruitment training will be organised for candidates from reserved categories who opt for it through the online application form.

How to Apply for Exim Bank Recruitment 2026

Candidates can apply online only, from 15 September 2026 to 10 October 2026. No other mode of application will be accepted.

  • Deputy Managers must execute a personal bond of ₹3 lakhs to serve the Bank for a minimum of 5 years from the date of joining.
  • Candidates who have defaulted on loan repayment or appear in the CIBIL defaulter database are not eligible to join the Bank.
  • Selected candidates already in service must produce a proper relieving letter/discharge certificate in original at the time of joining.
  • Any legal proceedings related to this advertisement can be instituted only in Mumbai, with courts/tribunals in Mumbai having sole and exclusive jurisdiction.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel, restrict, curtail, or enlarge the recruitment process, including the number of vacancies, at any stage without notice.
  • Candidates whose writing speed is permanently affected may use a scribe at their own cost and arrangement, subject to the Bank's stipulated scribe guidelines, and will be eligible for compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination if registered for it in advance.

Action against misconduct: Candidates found using unfair means, impersonation, misbehaviour in the examination/interview hall, disclosing or transmitting exam content, carrying mobile phones/electronic devices into the hall, or providing false information may be disqualified from the examination, debarred from future Bank examinations, or, if already employed, have their service terminated - in addition to being liable for criminal prosecution.

RRC NCR GDCE Eligibility Criteria

Who Can Apply for NCR GDCE 2026?

  • Eligible and serving regular employees (except RPF/RPSF) having lien in North Central Railway can apply against the GDCE quota.
  • All eligible regular and serving railway employees of NCR can fill the online application form. No minimum service condition is prescribed, as per RBE 72/2024 dated 02.08.2024.
  • Regular and eligible NCR employees who have the prescribed educational qualification for Direct Recruitment and work in grades lower than the grade/pay scale for which GDCE is being conducted can appear for all categories.
  • Regular and eligible employees with the prescribed educational qualification for Direct Recruitment who work in the same grade/pay scale for which GDCE is being conducted can appear for selection from Non-Safety to Safety category posts as well as Safety to Safety category posts.
  • Candidates must fulfil all notified eligibility criteria on or before the closing date for submission of the application.
  • Date of Birth and educational qualifications must be updated in the Service Records and in HRMS; otherwise the application is liable to be cancelled.

Who Cannot Apply for NCR GDCE 2026? (Non-Eligibility)

  • Employees in a higher grade than the grade of the notified post.
  • Employees who do not have the requisite educational qualification, medical standard and age criteria prescribed in the notification.
  • Trainee or Substitute employees who are not regularized.
  • RPF/RPSF personnel (as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)I/2002/PM2/9 dated 11.08.2003).
  • Law Assistant, Catering Inspector and Accounts Cadre (as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)I/2000/PN2/12 dated 21.08.2001, RBE No. 165/2001).
  • Candidates appearing in, or awaiting results of, the final examination for the minimum qualification at the time of applying.
  • Candidates who have resigned or been transferred from North Central Railway at any stage of the selection process.
  • Candidates are not allowed to apply for the same post on which they are presently working.

RRC NCR GDCE Qualification

Candidates must hold the minimum educational qualification for the post from a recognized Board/ University/ Institute as on the closing date for online application submission, as per Annexure-F. The qualification must also be endorsed in the Service Record of the employee, otherwise the candidature will be rejected. Those awaiting results of the final examination of the prescribed qualification should not apply.

  • The CBT has questions and answer options only in English and Hindi.
  • There is negative marking in the CBTs for all categories of posts: 1/3rd of the marks allotted for each question is deducted for each wrong answer.

ALP Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

  • Candidates equal to 8 (eight) times the number of ALP vacancies for each notified community/category (UR, OBC (NCL), SC, ST) are shortlisted for CBAT based on CBT marks. If more than one candidate obtains marks equal to the cut-off, all of them are shortlisted.
  • Each test battery/section of CBAT must be cleared separately. All candidates, irrespective of community, must secure a minimum T-score of 42 in each test battery separately, with no relaxation.
  • CBAT is only in English and Hindi, with no negative marking.
  • The merit list is prepared only from candidates qualifying in CBAT, with 50% weightage to CBT marks and 50% weightage to CBAT score (Railway Board's letter no. 2023/E(RRB)/25/38-A dated 16.04.2026).
  • For CBAT information, the notification refers candidates to the RDSO website (rdso.indianrailways.gov.in).

Computer Based Typing Skill Test (CBTST) for Junior Clerk cum Typist

The CBTST is of qualifying nature, and its marks are not added for merit. Candidates equal to eight times the number of vacancies for each community are called. Candidates should be able to type 30 words per minute (WPM) in English or 25 WPM in Hindi on a Personal Computer without editing tools and spell check. Kruti Dev and Mangal fonts are available for Hindi typing. Exemption may be extended to candidates permanently disabled due to Blindness/Low Vision, Cerebral Palsy and Locomotor Disability with not less than 40% permanent disability, who must upload or produce the Typing Skill Test Exemption Certificate issued by the Competent Medical Board before the test.

Minimum Qualifying Marks and Merit

Category Minimum Percentage of Marks
UR 40%
EWS 40%
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 30%
SC 30%
ST 25%
  • These percentages may be relaxed by 2% for PwBD candidates if there is a shortage of PwBD candidates against the vacancies reserved for them.
  • The marks scored in CBT are used for shortlisting candidates for further stages. Candidates equal to the number of vacancies are called for Document Verification, based on merit in CBT and the preference for post/exam group given.
  • Tie-break: the older candidate is placed higher in merit; if the age is also the same, alphabetical order (A to Z) of the name is used.
  • Normalization: raw marks are used for single-session papers and normalized marks for multi-session papers to compute a Merit Index. Merit Index = Sq + (St − Sq) × (M − Mq) / (Mt − Mq), where M is the marks obtained, Mq is the qualifying marks for the general category candidate (40), Mt is the mean marks of the top 0.1% or top 10 candidates (whichever is larger), Sq is 350 (score assigned to Mq) and St is 900 (score assigned to Mt).
  • A combined merit list of candidates from different disciplines/Exam Groups is prepared in descending order of the Merit Index, and allotment of preference is done on that basis.
  • Post/Unit is allotted as per the candidate's options, subject to merit, reservation policy and vacancy position on the date of finalizing the panel. Once empanelled, candidates forfeit the right to be considered for any other post/category.

RRC How to Apply for NCR GDCE Recruitment 2026

NCR GDCE Apply Online Steps

  1. Visit the official website of RRC/NCR, www.rrcpryj.org, and open the link for filling the application for GDCE Notification No. RRC/NCR/GDCE/01/2026.
  2. Click on the "New Registration" link.
  3. Fill in the personal information, e-mail address and mobile number. An e-mail/SMS will be received on the registered e-mail ID/mobile number with the registration number and password.
  4. Login using the registration number and password.
  5. Follow the instructions and complete the registration process step by step, including the post preference and exam group.
  6. Upload the scanned copy of the photograph, self-attested certificates in proof of date of birth, educational/technical qualifications and caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), and submit the application.

Name, Father's Name and Date of Birth must match the Matriculation or equivalent certificate as well as the service records. Candidates need not send printouts of the application or certificates to RRC by post.

Documents to Keep Ready and Upload

  • Proof of Date of Birth, and disability certificate for PwBD.
  • Certificate of Educational/Technical Qualification for the post applied.
  • For SC/ST candidates: Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-G.
  • For OBC candidates: valid Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-H, specifically indicating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer, plus the self-declaration as per Annexure-H (1).
  • Employee Service Certificate as per Annexure-I, filled by the applicant with signature and thumb impression (same as uploaded in the application) and verified by the immediate supervisor with signature, seal and mobile number.
  • Passport size colour photograph and specimen signature, in JPEG format.
  • The application also asks for Division/PU, Community, Employee ID No., Aadhar No., two visible marks of identification, and nearest Railway Station and Station Code.

Photograph and Signature Specifications

Item Specification
Photograph Colour passport size photograph, 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm, not older than three months, clear front view without cap and sunglasses; JPEG format, 100 DPI; file size 15 KB to 70 KB
Signature Signed on white paper with a black ink pen within a box of 50 mm x 20 mm; running handwriting, not block letters; JPG/JPEG, 100 DPI; 50 mm x 20 mm or 140 x 60 pixels (preferred); file size 10 KB to 40 KB

RRC NCR GDCE Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Applications are to be submitted online only through the link on www.rrcpryj.org. Candidates are advised to beware of fake websites and job racketeers. RRC does not appoint any agent or coaching centre for recruitment.
  • Candidates must have their own valid and active mobile number and personal e-mail ID for the entire examination process. RRC will not entertain any request to change the mobile number or e-mail ID after submission of the application.
  • Candidates should register well before the closing date to avoid last-minute load on the website. RRC will not bear responsibility if a candidate cannot register within the last date and time.
  • Post preference, once opted, is treated as final and no change is permissible. Candidates with partial options are considered only for the posts/categories they opted for. Not giving an option for certain posts/categories is treated as unwillingness for them.
  • Eligibility is considered only on the basis of information furnished in the online application. False or incorrect information or suppression of relevant information leads to rejection of candidature.
  • Candidates should note and preserve their Registration Number for further stages.
  • Signatures and photographs must be identical at all stages of the selection process. Candidates should keep at least 12 copies of the same photograph.
  • Candidates must ensure they meet the medical standards for the post. Appointment is subject to medical fitness, final verification of educational and community certificates, and verification of antecedents/character.
  • Selected employees are liable to be posted anywhere in North Central Railway, and the decision of the Railway administration is final.
  • Selection by RRC does not confer any right of appointment. RRC only recommends names to the concerned units of North Central Railway, which issue the offer of appointment letter.

Reasons for Rejection of Application

Applications are liable to be rejected on grounds including the following (the list is illustrative and not exhaustive):

  • Applications sent manually and not registered online.
  • More than one application by the same candidate for the same post. Candidates submitting multiple applications, including with minor changes in information, will be summarily rejected and debarred from all future examinations of RRBs and RRCs.
  • Not possessing the prescribed educational qualifications at the time of submitting the application.
  • Missing or improper scanned photograph, signature, LTI and other documents.
  • Invalid photographs (black and white, with cap or sunglasses/goggles, disfigured, small size, full body, one-side view, unrecognizable, photostat copy, group photo, selfie, photo taken by mobile, morphed photo, or no photo).
  • Signature in capital/block/disjointed letters.
  • Missing certificates in the prescribed format for date of birth, educational qualification and caste.
  • Incomplete or incorrectly filled applications.

If an application is rejected, candidates can view the status and reasons online on www.rrcpryj.org, and SMS/e-mail alerts are also sent. The decision is final and binding.

E-Call Letter, CBT and Document Verification Instructions

  • E-Call Letters are to be downloaded from the official website of RRC. No call letter is sent by post.
  • For the CBT, candidates must bring their Railway Identity card and a sparing letter (with the candidate's photo) bearing the signature and stamp of the concerned Supervisor/Controlling Officer, with the photo attested. Name, date of birth and photo on the ID must match the online application.
  • Candidates must bring the colour photograph (35 mm x 45 mm) uploaded with the application, and an original valid Photo ID.
  • Candidates must write the Self-Declaration paragraph, sign and affix LTI at the venue in the presence of the invigilator only. Writing it in advance or signing in capital letters leads to rejection.
  • Banned items inside the exam hall include mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, pen drives, laptops, calculators, wrist/smart watches, other communication devices, pen/pencil, wallets/purses, belts, shoes and metallic wear including ornaments.
  • For Document Verification, candidates must bring all required documents in original, along with two sets of self-attested photocopies. Certificates must be in English or Hindi in the prescribed formats. Candidates absent during Document Verification will have their candidature cancelled.
  • Candidates who want to be considered against reserved vacancies or seek age relaxation must submit the relevant original certificate in the prescribed format at Document Verification; otherwise they will be considered under General (UR) if eligible.

Malpractice and Impersonation Warning

Any candidate using unfair means, sending someone else in their place or attempting to impersonate will be debarred from all examinations of all RRCs and RRBs for lifetime, in addition to departmental disciplinary action and possible legal prosecution. The notification refers to The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act and Rules, 2024, as amended on 31.07.2026. RRC may conduct post-examination analysis including log analysis, photograph and biometric verification and CCTV footage review.

How to Download the RRB Technician City Intimation Slip 2026

You can check your exam city online through the RRB login page. Keep your registration number and date of birth ready.

  1. Open the direct city intimation login link given under Important Links.
  2. Under Candidate Login, enter your registration number.
  3. Enter your password, which is your date of birth in DD/MM/YYYY format (for example, 26/01/1990).
  4. Type the captcha code carefully and click Login.
  5. Your city intimation slip appears on the screen.
  6. Check your exam city, state, exam date and shift, then download or save the slip for reference.

What to do if you cannot log in

  • Recheck your registration number and enter your date of birth in DD/MM/YYYY format.
  • Check the captcha carefully and refresh it if it is unclear.
  • Clear your browser cache and cookies, or try a private or incognito window.
  • Switch to another browser such as Chrome or Firefox, preferably on a laptop or desktop.
  • If the page is slow, try again later, since heavy traffic is common on release days.
  • Disable any pop-up blocker in case the slip opens in a new tab.

Details to Check on the RRB Technician Exam City Slip

After downloading the slip, verify these details. The sources reviewed do not fully agree on whether the reporting time and gate closing time appear on the city slip itself, so confirm them from the e-call letter.

Detail Why It Matters
Candidate name and registration number Confirms the slip belongs to you
Exam city and state Helps you plan travel and stay
Exam date Falls within 6 to 9 October 2026
Shift timing Tells you which shift you are allotted
Reporting time and gate closing time Reported on the slip by one source; confirm on the e-call letter
Instructions Aadhaar, ID and exam-day rules

Important Instructions for RRB Technician Candidates

  • The city slip is not your e-call letter and does not permit you to appear in the exam.
  • As stated in the instructions on the slip, there will be no change of exam date, city, shift or centre under any circumstances.
  • Carry your Aadhaar card along with other ID proof. Aadhaar-enabled biometric verification will be done at the exam centre.
  • Authenticate your Aadhaar by logging in at rrbapply.gov.in beforehand, if not already done, even if you verified it at the application stage.
  • Keep your Aadhaar unlocked in the UIDAI system before you reach the exam centre.
  • Your Aadhaar should carry the correct name, date of birth (as per Class 10 certificate), latest photograph, biometrics (if not updated after age 15), address and father's name.
  • Follow only official RRB websites for updates and avoid touts who promise jobs for money. Selection is based on CBT merit.

What Happens After the City Intimation Slip?

  1. City intimation slip (released 27 September 2026)
  2. E-call letter (about 4 days before your exam date)
  3. Computer Based Test (6 to 9 October 2026)
  4. Document Verification
  5. Medical Examination

The last date to raise objections is 24/09/2026. The objection window opened on 21/09/2026, so candidates have four days in total, including the release day. The closing time on the last day is Not Available on the portal pages checked, so submit your objections well before 24/09/2026.

How to Check the MPESB AEO Answer Key 2026

  1. Visit the official website esb.mp.gov.in, or open the Group-2 Sub Group-1 exam portal from the Important Links table below.
  2. On the exam portal, click Objection Tracker Login.
  3. Enter your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format. For example, 01 February 1990 is entered as 01021990.
  4. Fill in the other login details shown on the page and enter the captcha.
  5. Log in and follow the on-screen options to view your details and the answer key.
  6. Save or print the page or PDF for future reference.

How to Raise an Objection Against the MPESB AEO Answer Key

  1. Log in to the Objection Tracker between 21/09/2026 and 24/09/2026.
  2. Find the question you want to challenge.
  3. Submit your objection following the instructions displayed on the portal.
  4. Complete any fee payment the portal asks for, and save the acknowledgement.

The objection fee for this exam is Not Available in the pages checked, so read the portal instructions before you submit. For comparison, the Board charged ₹50 per question in the March 2026 ITI Training Officer answer key. That was a different recruitment, so do not treat it as the AEO fee.

How to Calculate Your Score Using the Answer Key

  1. Note down your responses and compare each one with the answer key.
  2. Count the correct, wrong and unattempted questions.
  3. Add the marks for correct answers as given in the official marking scheme.
  4. Deduct 0.25 marks for each wrong answer, the negative marking reported for this exam.

Estimated score = (Correct answers × marks per correct answer) − (Wrong answers × 0.25). The marks per correct answer are not confirmed in the sources checked, so verify them in the official notification. Since the first key is provisional, your final score may change if the Board revises any answer.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Submit all objections on or before 24/09/2026.
  • Keep your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format and your application details ready before logging in.
  • Save the acknowledgement of every objection you submit.
  • The first answer key is provisional, and the Board may revise it after objections.
  • Check the Board's notices regularly for the final answer key and result.

RRB Group D (Level 1) Recruitment 2026 : Document Required

Photo & Signature
  • The candidate’s photograph must be a recent passport-sized photograph and must be clear or white. The face must be clearly visible and the candidate must not be wearing a hat, glasses, or mask.
  • The signature should be made in black on white paper and should be clear and easily readable.
Aadhaar Card
  • Aadhaar number is required while filling the form, and it is mandatory to produce the original Aadhaar card during PET and document verification.
10th Class Marksheet
  • This document is used as a certificate of date of birth and educational qualification.
Caste / Category Certificates (If Applicable)
  • Candidates must have a valid SC/ST certificate, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate, or EWS certificate for the current financial year. The certificate must be issued in the format prescribed by the government.
PwBD / Disability Certificate (If Applicable)
  • The person with disability must have a disability certificate issued by a special medical board clearly stating the percentage of disability.
Ex-Serviceman Certificate (If Applicable)
  • Candidates must possess a valid Discharge Book or Service Certificate, in which the length of service is clearly mentioned.
Bank Account Details
  • Candidates must provide the account holder’s name, account number, and IFSC code, which are required for fee refund or future payments.
Domicile / Address Proof (If Asked)
  • Candidates may need to provide a state domicile certificate along with their permanent and correspondence address details, if required.
Other Useful Documents
  • Candidates must keep an active email ID and mobile number, along with the application/confirmation page printout and fee payment receipt, for future reference.
Note : Candidates must Keep all documents scanned and ready before form filling. Fill name, DOB, and parents’ names exactly as per 10th marksheet. Incorrect or fake documents can cancel selection. Carry originals with self-attested photocopies for verification.
